The shoulder blades are visibly retracted and squeezed together, creating prominent definition across the upper back and rear deltoids, with the chest lifted and shoulders drawn back.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Shoulder External Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a resistance band at chest height with elbow bent 90 degrees at your side. Band is looped around hands.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your forearm outward against band resistance, keeping elbow stationary at your side. Hold briefly, then return to start position.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Shoulder Internal Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding resistance band with elbow bent 90 degrees and forearm rotated outward. Band is anchored at chest height.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your forearm inward against band resistance, keeping elbow stationary. Hold briefly, then return to start position.

exercises.name: Resisted Ankle Dorsiflexion
exercises.pose_description: Seated or standing with a resistance band looped around the top of the forefoot, anchored to a fixed point in front. The foot pulls upward against the band resistance, dorsiflexing the ankle and bringing the toes toward the shin. The heel remains on the floor and the lower leg stays stationary.
exercises.end_pose_description: The foot is maximally dorsiflexed with toes pulled sharply toward the shin at approximately 20-30 degrees upward from neutral, while the heel remains planted on the floor and the lower leg stays vertical and stationary. The anterior tibialis muscle on the front of the shin appears visibly engaged and contracted, creating visible definition along the front of the lower leg. The resistance band is at maximum stretch tension across the top of the forefoot.

exercises.name: Resisted Ankle Plantarflexion
exercises.pose_description: Seated or standing with a resistance band looped around the ball of the foot, anchored behind the body or held in the hands. The foot pushes downward against the band resistance, plantarflexing the ankle and pointing the toes. The lower leg stays stationary and the movement occurs purely at the ankle.
exercises.end_pose_description: The foot is maximally plantarflexed with toes pointed downward at approximately 45-60 degrees below the horizontal plane, while the lower leg remains completely stationary and vertical. The calf muscle is visibly contracted and tightened, the resistance band is stretched taut beneath the ball of the foot, and the upper body remains upright and stable with no compensatory movement.

exercises.name: Resisted Back Extension with Band
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and a resistance band looped around a fixed point at chest height in front of you. Hold both ends of the band with arms extended forward at chest level, maintaining neutral spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull the band toward your torso by squeezing your shoulder blades together and extending your thoracic spine slightly backward. Hold this retracted position while keeping your core engaged and lower back neutral.

exercises.name: Resisted Foot Eversion in Side-Lying
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your unaffected side with your bottom leg bent for stability and your top leg extended. Loop the band around both feet just above the toes.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lift your top foot upward and outward against the band resistance, isolating the peroneal muscles. Lower with control and repeat.

exercises.name: Reverse Wrist Curl with Dumbbell
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your forearm resting on a table, palm facing upward, holding a light dumbbell. Your wrist hangs slightly beyond the edge with the dumbbell at the starting position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Curl your wrist upward, lifting the dumbbell toward your body using only wrist motion. Pause briefly at the top before lowering the weight back to the starting position.

exercises.name: Reverse Wrist Curls
exercises.pose_description: Seated or standing with the forearm resting on a table or thigh, palm facing down, holding a light dumbbell. The wrist extends upward, lifting the back of the hand toward the ceiling while the forearm remains stationary. The movement is small and controlled, targeting the wrist extensors.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is seated with their forearm flat and stable on a table or thigh, palm facing downward, while the hand is fully extended upward at the wrist with fingers pointing toward the ceiling—the wrist is at maximum extension. The forearm remains completely still and neutral, highlighting the engaged wrist extensor muscles on the top of the forearm, while the dumbbell is held at the highest point of the movement with the back of the hand elevated.

exercises.name: Scalene Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with good posture and feet flat on the floor. Keep your shoulders relaxed and your head in a neutral position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Tilt your head toward one shoulder while gently pulling the opposite shoulder down with your hand. Feel a stretch along the side of your neck and upper shoulder.

exercises.name: Scapular Retraction with Band
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a resistance band at chest height with both hands in front of you. Your arms are extended forward with a slight bend in the elbows and the band is taut.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull the band toward your chest by squeezing your shoulder blades together, keeping your elbows high and level with your shoulders. Your chest is open and your posture is upright at the end of the movement.

exercises.name: Scapular Retraction Squeeze
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with arms at your sides, shoulders relaxed. Keep your chest open and spine neutral.
exercises.end_pose_description: Squeeze your shoulder blades together and slightly down, retracting them toward your spine. Hold the contraction while keeping arms relaxed at sides.

exercises.name: Scapular Retractions with Resistance
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with your arms extended forward at shoulder height, palms facing each other. Your core is engaged and shoulders are relaxed.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull your arms backward, squeezing your shoulder blades together as if trying to hold a pencil between them. Return slowly to the starting position with control.

exercises.name: Scapular Squeeze with Band
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a looped resistance band at chest height with arms extended at shoulder width. Maintain neutral spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull band outward by squeezing shoulder blades together, keeping arms at shoulder height. Hold briefly, then return to start with controlled motion.

exercises.name: Scapular Squeezes
exercises.pose_description: A person is seated upright with good posture, maintaining a straight back. Shoulders are relaxed and positioned naturally, with arms hanging loosely at the sides. The head is in a neutral position with the chin slightly tucked.
exercises.end_pose_description: Standing upright. The shoulder blades are squeezed maximally together behind the back. The chest is pushed forward and open. The shoulders are pulled back. Both arms are at the sides with elbows slightly bent.

exercises.name: Sciatic Nerve Glide
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with one hip and knee bent to 90 degrees, hands clasping behind the thigh. The knee slowly straightens, extending the foot toward the ceiling while the ankle alternates between dorsiflexion and plantarflexion to glide the sciatic nerve. The opposite leg remains flat on the floor, and the movement is smooth and pain-free.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine on their back with the working leg extended nearly straight toward the ceiling (knee at approximately 10-20 degrees of flexion), foot positioned with the ankle in dorsiflexion (toes pointing toward the face), while the clasped hands remain behind the thigh providing gentle support. The non-working leg remains flat and relaxed on the floor, and the person's torso and head stay neutral against the ground with minimal movement.

exercises.name: Seated Adductor Squeeze with Band
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Place a resistance band between your knees, just above them, ensuring it is held firmly in place.
exercises.end_pose_description: Squeeze your knees together against the band resistance, engaging the inner thigh muscles. Maintain the squeeze for 2 seconds before releasing.

exercises.name: Seated Ankle Dorsiflexion with Band
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with your leg extended, a resistance band looped around the ball of your foot. Keep your knee straight and stable.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull your toes toward your shin against the resistance of the band, creating tension in the front of the ankle. Hold briefly at the top of the range of motion.

exercises.name: Seated Ankle Inversion and Eversion
exercises.pose_description: Sit in a chair with your injured leg extended out in front of you or resting on another chair. Keep your knee relaxed and your foot in a neutral position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly rotate your foot inward (inversion) so the sole of your foot faces toward your other leg, then rotate outward (eversion) so the sole faces away. Move through the full comfortable range of motion without forcing.

exercises.name: Seated Ankle Inversion with Band
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your legs extended in front of you on the floor or a bench. Loop a resistance band around the ball of your foot, holding both ends with your hands.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull your foot inward (inversion) against the band resistance, creating tension through the peroneal tendons. Hold briefly at the end range of motion.

exercises.name: Seated Ankle Pumps
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair or on a bed with legs extended in front or feet hanging off the edge. The ankles alternately pump up and down, dorsiflexing to pull the toes toward the shins, then plantarflexing to point the toes away. The movement is rhythmic and continuous, promoting circulation and ankle mobility.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person sits upright in the chair with one foot plantarflexed (toes pointed away from the body, heel anchored) while the other foot is dorsiflexed (toes pulled up toward the shin). The calf muscles of the plantarflexed leg appear engaged and tightened, while the shin muscles of the dorsiflexed leg show tension. The torso remains stable and upright against the chair back, with arms resting naturally.

exercises.name: Seated Anterior Tibialis Strengthening
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with your feet flat on the floor. Place a light dumbbell on the top of one foot near the toes, or use a resistance band looped around the ball of your foot.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull your toes upward toward your shin against the resistance, engaging the muscles along the front of your lower leg. Hold briefly and lower back down with control.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raises
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair with feet flat on the floor and knees bent at 90 degrees. The heels lift off the ground as high as possible, pushing up onto the balls of the feet while the toes remain on the floor. Additional weight may be placed on the knees for resistance. The movement is controlled up and down.
exercises.end_pose_description: Seated on a chair with feet on the ground. Both heels are lifted high off the ground, rising up onto the balls of the feet. The calf muscles are visibly contracted. Knees are bent at 90 degrees.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with one leg extended in front of you and the other bent with foot on the floor. Keep your back upright against the chair.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lean forward slightly and pull your extended foot's toes toward your shin, feeling a stretch along the back of your calf and Achilles tendon. Maintain the stretch for 20-30 seconds.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Stretches
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair. Extend one leg forward with the heel resting on the floor and the toes pointed towards the ceiling. The other foot remains flat on the floor with the knee bent at approximately 90 degrees.
exercises.end_pose_description: Extend one leg straight out in front of you and gently pull your toes back toward your shin using a towel or your hand. Hold the stretch feeling it through your calf and foot.

exercises.name: Seated Cervical Retraction
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair with good upright posture, shoulders relaxed, and feet flat on the floor. The chin draws straight backward in a horizontal motion, creating a double chin, without tilting the head up or down. The movement retracts the cervical spine, strengthening the deep neck flexors. The gaze remains level throughout.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person sits upright with their head pulled straight back horizontally, chin tucked inward creating a pronounced double chin, while the gaze remains forward and level. The neck and upper back muscles are visibly engaged and contracted, with the cervical spine in full retraction. The shoulders remain relaxed and level, the spine maintains neutral alignment, and feet stay flat on the floor.

exercises.name: Seated Doorway Chest Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair next to a doorframe with your affected arm at 90-degree shoulder abduction, elbow bent, and forearm resting against the doorframe. Your upper arm is parallel to the ground.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently rotate your torso forward and away from the doorframe, creating a mild stretch across your chest and front shoulder. Hold this position for 20-30 seconds while breathing steadily, keeping the stretch comfortable and pain-free.

exercises.name: Seated Dorsiflexion with Resistance Band
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with one leg extended and a resistance band looped around the ball of your foot, holding the band ends in both hands. Keep your knee slightly bent.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull your toes toward your shin against the band resistance, creating tension in your shin muscles. Hold the contraction briefly before returning to the start position.

exercises.name: Seated Figure Four Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair with good posture. One ankle is crossed over the opposite knee in a figure-four position, with the crossed knee dropping open to the side. The torso leans gently forward from the hips until a stretch is felt in the outer hip and glute of the crossed leg. Hands may rest on the shin of the crossed leg.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person sits upright in a chair with one ankle crossed over the opposite knee, creating a 90-degree angle at the hip with the crossed knee dropped open laterally. The torso is folded forward from the hips at approximately 30-45 degrees, with the spine maintaining a gentle curve as hands rest on or near the shin of the crossed leg, while the glute and external rotator muscles of the crossed leg appear engaged and stretched. The head remains in neutral alignment with the spine, and the person faces forward or slightly downward.

exercises.name: Seated Foot Alphabet
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with one leg extended or slightly raised, keeping the foot relaxed. Your knee is straight and the foot is positioned in front of you as if writing on an imaginary surface.
exercises.end_pose_description: Use your entire foot to trace the letters of the alphabet in the air, engaging all foot muscles through various ranges of motion. Continue through the entire alphabet to improve foot mobility and control.

exercises.name: Seated Foot Inversion with Resistance Band
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with your feet flat on the floor. Loop a resistance band around the ball of your foot with the other end anchored to a stable object at ankle height on the inside of your foot.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly turn the sole of your foot inward (inversion), creating tension against the resistance band. Hold for 1-2 seconds at the end range of motion while maintaining control.

exercises.name: Seated Gastrocnemius Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with both legs extended in front of you. Loop a resistance band around one forefoot while keeping that knee straight.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently pull the band to bring your toes toward your shin, stretching the calf muscle. Hold for 30-45 seconds without bouncing.

exercises.name: Seated Glute Squeezes
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a firm chair with your back supported and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Keep your hands resting on your thighs.
exercises.end_pose_description: Squeeze your glute muscles as tightly as possible, holding the contraction for 2-3 seconds. Release and relax, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Seated Hamstring Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Sitting on the ground (NOT on a chair or bench) with one leg extended straight forward. The other knee is bent to the side. The person bends forward at the waist reaching both hands toward the foot of the straight leg to stretch the hamstring.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is seated on the ground with their torso folded forward at approximately 45-90 degrees toward an extended straight leg, hands clasped or reaching toward the foot/shin of the extended leg, while the opposite leg remains bent with knee out to the side. The extended leg is fully straight with minimal knee bend, the hamstring and calf muscles appear elongated and engaged, and the spine shows flexion as the person leans deeply into the stretch.

exercises.name: Seated Hip External Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with your injured leg crossed over your opposite knee, forming a figure-4 position. Keep your back straight and posture neutral.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently lean forward from the hips to deepen the stretch on the outer hip and glute of the crossed leg. Maintain steady breathing and hold the position without bouncing.

exercises.name: Seated Hip Internal Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with both feet flat on the floor and knees bent to 90 degrees. Keep your back straight and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly rotate one knee inward across the body, internally rotating at the hip joint while keeping your foot off the floor. Return to center and repeat on the opposite side.

exercises.name: Seated Hip Internal Rotation Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with both feet flat on the floor and good posture. Keep your core gently engaged and shoulders relaxed.
exercises.end_pose_description: Cross one ankle over the opposite knee and gently press the raised knee downward while leaning slightly forward. Feel the stretch in the outer hip and glute of the raised leg.

exercises.name: Seated Hip Internal Rotation Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright on the floor with one leg extended and the other knee bent, foot placed on the outside of the extended knee. Keep your back straight and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently twist your torso toward the bent knee, using your opposite arm to increase the stretch. Hold the position while maintaining an upright posture.

exercises.name: Seated Knee Extension
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair with feet flat on the floor and knees bent at 90 degrees. One leg extends straight out in front by straightening the knee until the leg is parallel with the floor, engaging the quadriceps. The thigh remains on the seat, the back stays against the chair, and the movement is controlled both up and down.
exercises.end_pose_description: Seated on a chair or bench. The right leg is extended fully forward, straight and parallel to the floor. The knee is locked. The quadriceps muscle is visibly engaged. The left foot remains flat on the ground.

exercises.name: Seated Long Sitting Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Seated on the floor with both legs extended straight in front, feet together and toes pointing up. The torso hinges forward from the hips, reaching both hands toward the toes while keeping the back as flat as possible. The knees remain pressed into the floor, and the stretch is felt along the hamstrings and lower back.
exercises.end_pose_description: The torso is folded forward at the hips with the head positioned near or toward the shins, arms extended straight alongside or grasping the legs/feet, and the back forms a continuous rounded curve from the shoulders to the lower back. Both legs remain fully extended and pressed flat against the floor with knees locked straight, feet flexed with toes pointing upward, creating maximum length through the posterior chain from the hamstrings to the upper back.

exercises.name: Seated Marching
exercises.pose_description: Sit in a firm chair with your back against the backrest and both feet flat on the floor. Keep your posture upright and relaxed.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly lift the affected knee up toward the chest in a marching motion while keeping the other foot on the floor. Lower back down and repeat in a controlled, rhythmic manner.

exercises.name: Seated Posture Micro-Practice
exercises.pose_description: Seated upright in a chair with feet flat on the floor. Spine tall and neutral, shoulders rolled back and down, chin slightly tucked. Hands resting on thighs. Demonstrating ideal seated posture alignment with a subtle glow or highlight along the spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains seated upright with spine fully extended and neutral, shoulders actively drawn back and down creating visible scapular retraction, chest lifted and open, chin parallel to the ground with a subtle tuck, and hands resting naturally on the thighs with arms at roughly 90-degree angles. The entire posterior chain—erector spinae, rhomboids, and upper back muscles—appears engaged and highlighted, with the torso forming a vertical line from the crown of the head through the pelvis. The person faces directly forward with eyes ahead, feet planted flat on the floor hip-width apart.

exercises.name: Seated Row with Band
exercises.pose_description: Seated on the floor with legs extended straight in front and a resistance band looped around the feet. Both hands grip the band with palms facing each other. The elbows pull straight back, squeezing the shoulder blades together, drawing the hands toward the lower ribs. The torso remains upright and does not lean backward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is seated upright with legs extended straight, elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees and pulled tightly against the ribcage, with hands drawn back toward the lower chest/ribs while maintaining a neutral spine. The shoulder blades are visibly retracted and squeezed together, the chest is slightly puffed forward, and the back musculature (lats and rhomboids) appears maximally contracted and engaged. The resistance band remains taut between the looped feet and the hands at the end position.

exercises.name: Seated Shoulder Abduction
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright on a bench with your back against support and feet flat on the floor. Hold light dumbbells at your sides with arms hanging down and elbows slightly bent.
exercises.end_pose_description: Raise both arms out to the sides in a wide arc until your upper arms are parallel to the ground, forming a T-shape with your body. Lower back down slowly with control.

exercises.name: Seated Shoulder Press
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair with back supported and feet flat on the floor. Dumbbells or a resistance band are held at shoulder height with elbows bent and palms facing forward. The arms press straight overhead until fully extended, then lower back to shoulder height. The back remains against the chair and the core is engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person sits upright with their back firmly against the chair, arms fully extended overhead with elbows locked straight, dumbbells or resistance band held at arm's length above shoulder width. The shoulders are elevated and engaged, pressing upward, while the core appears braced with the torso stable and vertical. The face looks forward with visible tension through the shoulders, upper back, and triceps.

exercises.name: Seated Shoulder Shrugs
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a sturdy chair with feet flat on the floor and arms resting at your sides with palms facing inward. Maintain good posture with shoulders relaxed in their neutral position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Raise both shoulders up toward your ears in a shrugging motion, holding the elevated position for 2 seconds. Lower your shoulders back down in a controlled manner to the starting position.

exercises.name: Seated Shoulder Shrugs with Dumbbell
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with good posture and feet flat on the floor. Hold a light dumbbell in each hand with arms at your sides and shoulders in a neutral, relaxed position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Elevate both shoulders toward your ears by contracting your trapezius muscles. Hold briefly at the top, then lower slowly back to the starting position with control.

exercises.name: Seated Spinal Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with feet flat on the floor and good posture, keeping your hips and pelvis stable. Cross your arms over your chest or place hands behind your head.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently rotate your upper spine and torso to one side, feeling a controlled stretch through the mid-back. Keep your hips still and return to center before rotating to the other side.

exercises.name: Seated Spinal Stretch with Band
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright on the floor with legs extended in front of you. Loop a resistance band around both feet and hold the ends loosely in your hands.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently fold forward at the hips while keeping your back straight, using the band to deepen the stretch along your hamstrings and lower back. Hold this position and breathe deeply.

exercises.name: Seated Spinal Twist
exercises.pose_description: Seated on the floor with one leg extended straight and the other leg crossed over with the foot flat on the floor outside the opposite knee. The torso rotates toward the bent knee, and the opposite elbow hooks outside the bent knee for leverage. The sitting bones remain grounded, the spine stays tall, and the rotation comes from the thoracic and lumbar spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: The torso is rotated maximally toward the bent knee, with the spine twisted from the thoracic spine, while the head follows the rotation to gaze over the shoulder. The hooked elbow presses against the outside of the bent knee for leverage, the extended leg remains straight on the floor, the opposite arm reaches behind for balance or wraps around the torso, and the sitting bones stay planted as the obliques and spinal rotators appear fully engaged and lengthened on the extended side.

exercises.name: Seated Tibialis Posterior Activation with Towel
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with a small towel laid out flat on the floor in front of you. Place the ball of your foot on one end of the towel.
exercises.end_pose_description: Using only your foot and toes, curl the towel toward you by scrunching your toes and engaging the tibialis posterior and intrinsic foot muscles. Relax and repeat, gradually pulling the entire towel under your foot.

exercises.name: Seated Toe Taps
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair with feet flat on the floor and knees bent at 90 degrees. The toes lift off the floor while the heels remain planted, then the toes tap back down. The movement alternates between feet or both feet tap simultaneously, working the tibialis anterior and ankle dorsiflexors in a rhythmic motion.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains seated upright in the chair with knees bent at 90 degrees, while the toes are maximally lifted off the floor with the balls of the feet raised as high as possible, creating a pronounced dorsiflexion angle at the ankles. The heels stay firmly planted on the ground, and the tibialis anterior muscles along the front of the shins appear visibly contracted and engaged. The torso remains stable and upright against the chair back.

exercises.name: Seated Trunk Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair with feet flat on the floor and knees bent at 90 degrees. A stick, band, or the arms crossed over the chest provide a reference. The torso rotates to one side as far as comfortably possible, then returns to center and rotates to the other side. The hips and knees remain fixed forward while the rotation comes from the thoracic and lumbar spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: The seated figure is rotated maximally to one side with the torso twisted at approximately 45-90 degrees from center, while the hips and lower body remain square to the front with feet flat and knees bent at 90 degrees. The arms are either crossed over the chest or holding a stick/band parallel to the shoulders, pointing perpendicular to the direction the torso faces. The oblique and spinal rotator muscles on the rotating side appear engaged and shortened, while those on the opposite side appear lengthened and stretched.

exercises.name: Seated Upper Back Posture Reset
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with feet flat, hands clasped behind your head with elbows out to the sides. Maintain a neutral spine position without arching your lower back.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently draw your elbows backward while opening your chest, creating a mild extension through your upper back without straining. Hold for 2 seconds while taking a deep breath, then relax back to neutral.

exercises.name: Seated Upper Back Squeeze
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with feet flat on the floor and arms at your sides with elbows bent at 90 degrees. Keep shoulders relaxed and chest lifted.
exercises.end_pose_description: Squeeze your shoulder blades together as if trying to hold a pencil between them, engaging the muscles of the upper back. Release and repeat without rounding your shoulders forward.

exercises.name: Serratus Anterior Punch (Prone)
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on a flat bench with your chest and abdomen supported, and your head in a neutral position. Hold a light dumbbell in each hand with your arms extended forward, elbows slightly bent, and your hands positioned in front of your shoulders, just above the bench surface.
exercises.end_pose_description: Punch the dumbbells forward while allowing your shoulder blades to protract and spread across your ribcage. This motion emphasizes serratus anterior activation without rotating your torso.

exercises.name: Short Arc Quads
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with a bolster or rolled towel placed under one knee, supporting it in approximately 20 to 30 degrees of flexion. The lower leg straightens fully by extending the knee, lifting the foot off the floor while the thigh stays on the bolster. The quadriceps contract to lock the knee straight, and the ankle is dorsiflexed.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains supine on their back with one knee fully extended and locked straight, the foot lifted several inches off the floor with the toes pointing upward (dorsiflexed ankle), while the thigh remains supported on the bolster beneath it. The quadriceps muscle on the extended leg appears visibly contracted and taut from hip to knee, creating a defined line along the front of the thigh. The opposite leg remains relaxed on the floor, and the torso stays flat against the ground.

exercises.name: Short Foot Exercise
exercises.pose_description: Sit in a chair with your bare foot flat on the floor in a neutral position. Your toes are relaxed and extended naturally.
exercises.end_pose_description: Shorten your foot by engaging the arch and drawing the ball of your foot toward your heel without curling your toes. Hold this contraction briefly, feeling the arch muscles engage and lift slightly.

exercises.name: Shoulder Abduction
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with arms at sides. One arm lifts straight out to the side, away from the body, with the elbow straight and palm facing down, rising to shoulder height or above. The torso remains tall and does not lean to the opposite side, and the shoulder does not shrug upward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with one arm extended fully straight out to the side at shoulder height (90-degree abduction), palm facing downward, while the opposite arm remains at their side. The torso is perfectly vertical with no lateral lean, the shoulder of the raised arm is packed down (not shrugged), and the deltoid and upper back muscles appear visibly engaged and contracted.

exercises.name: Shoulder Blade Squeezes
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with your arms at your sides, elbows bent to 90 degrees. Keep your shoulders relaxed away from your ears.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull your shoulder blades backward and down, squeezing the muscles between your shoulder blades together. Hold briefly while maintaining an upright posture.

exercises.name: Shoulder Flexion
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with arms at sides, holding a light weight or no weight. One arm lifts straight forward and upward in front of the body with the elbow straight, palm facing down, reaching toward the ceiling in full shoulder flexion. The torso stays upright without arching the back, and the shoulder blade glides naturally along the ribcage.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with one arm fully extended straight overhead at approximately 180 degrees of shoulder flexion, elbow locked straight, palm facing inward or forward, with the arm aligned vertically above the shoulder. The torso remains neutral and upright with no spinal arch, while the opposite arm hangs relaxed at the side, and the anterior deltoid, clavicular head of pectoralis major, and serratus anterior are visibly engaged.

exercises.name: Shoulder Shrugs
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright, facing forward, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Arms hang straight down at the sides, palms facing inward, and shoulders are relaxed.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with arms hanging straight down at their sides, shoulders elevated maximally toward the ears in a shrugged position, creating visible tension and bulging in the upper trapezius and neck region. The head remains in neutral position with no forward tilt or rotation, and the entire upper body appears rigid with the shrug contracted at its highest point.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Clamshell with Band
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your side with hips and knees bent at 45 degrees, a resistance band looped around both thighs just above the knees. Keep your feet together and your bottom arm supporting your head.
exercises.end_pose_description: Open your top knee against the band resistance while keeping your feet together and hips stable. Pause at the top before slowly returning to the starting position.

exercises.name: Side-Lying External Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Lying on the uninvolved side with the working arm on top. The elbow of the top arm is bent to 90 degrees and pinned against the side with a small towel roll between the elbow and the ribcage. A light dumbbell is held in the hand, and the forearm rotates upward toward the ceiling, externally rotating the shoulder. The elbow remains stationary throughout.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies on their side with the working arm's elbow still bent at 90 degrees and anchored against the ribcage, while the forearm is rotated upward so the dumbbell points toward the ceiling, creating a vertical line from elbow to hand. The shoulder is externally rotated maximally, with the posterior shoulder and rotator cuff muscles visibly engaged and contracted. The torso remains stable and flat against the ground, perpendicular to the floor.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
exercises.pose_description: Lying on one side with the body in a straight line, bottom arm extended under the head for support. The top leg lifts straight upward toward the ceiling to approximately 30 to 45 degrees while keeping the knee straight and toes pointed forward. The hips remain stacked and do not roll forward or backward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies on their side in a straight line, with the top leg raised to approximately 45-60 degrees from the body, knee fully extended and toes pointed forward, while the bottom leg remains straight on the ground. The torso stays upright and stacked vertically above the bottom leg, with the bottom arm extended under the head and the top arm resting along the side of the torso. The abductor muscles on the outer hip and thigh of the top leg are visibly contracted and engaged, creating a defined line from hip to knee.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Shoulder Abduction
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your unaffected side with your bottom arm bent for support and your head resting comfortably. Your affected arm should rest on your side with a slight bend in the elbow.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lift your affected arm up toward the ceiling in a controlled motion, keeping your torso stable and avoiding any rolling backward. Lower the arm back down with control.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Shoulder Internal Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your unaffected side with your affected shoulder abducted to 90 degrees and elbow bent to 90 degrees. Hold a light dumbbell in your affected hand with your forearm pointing upward.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your forearm downward toward your torso, moving only at the shoulder's internal rotators. Keep your elbow fixed and shoulder stable throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.pose_description: Body supported on one forearm and the side of the bottom foot, forming a straight line from head to feet. The supporting elbow is directly under the shoulder, the top arm rests on the hip or extends toward the ceiling. The hips are lifted high and do not sag toward the floor, and the core is fully engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body forms a perfectly straight diagonal line from head to feet, balanced on the supporting forearm (elbow bent 90 degrees directly beneath the shoulder) and the outer edge of the bottom foot, with hips lifted high and aligned with shoulders and ankles. The top leg is fully extended and stacked directly over the bottom leg, while the top arm either rests along the torso or extends upward, with the entire lateral core, obliques, and shoulder stabilizers visibly contracted and tensioned. The head maintains neutral alignment with the spine, facing forward, with no sagging at the hips or rotation of the torso.

exercises.name: Sidelying Hip Abduction
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your side with your body in a straight line, legs stacked, and your head resting on your lower arm. Keep your core engaged and your pelvis stable throughout the movement.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lift your top leg toward the ceiling to about 45 degrees, keeping your torso still and avoiding rolling backward. Lower the leg with control without letting it touch the bottom leg.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Overhead Press
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a dumbbell at shoulder height with your elbow slightly in front of your body. Your core is braced and your scapulae are packed.
exercises.end_pose_description: Press the dumbbell overhead in a slight forward angle, allowing your scapula to upwardly rotate naturally at the end. Your arm is fully extended with controlled stability throughout the entire range of motion.

exercises.name: Single Leg Balance
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright on one leg with the standing knee slightly soft, not locked. The opposite foot is lifted a few inches off the ground with the knee bent. Arms can be at sides or extended for balance, torso is upright, and the gaze is directed forward at a fixed point.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands vertically balanced on one leg with a slightly bent knee, while the opposite leg is lifted with the knee bent at approximately 90 degrees and the thigh parallel to the ground. The torso remains upright and centered over the standing leg, with visible core engagement, while the arms are either extended outward at shoulder height or positioned for counterbalance, and the head faces forward with eyes fixed on a point ahead.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Balance with Hip Activation
exercises.pose_description: Standing on one leg with the standing knee slightly soft and the hip of the standing leg actively engaged. The non-standing leg lifts with the knee bent and the hip moves through small ranges of flexion, extension, or abduction to challenge balance. Arms may be at sides or on hips, the torso is upright, and the gaze is fixed on a point ahead.
exercises.end_pose_description: The camera captures a figure standing tall on one straight leg with the standing hip and glute visibly engaged and stable, while the non-standing leg is lifted with the knee bent at approximately 90 degrees and the hip abducted, extended, or flexed to its endpoint depending on the movement pattern. The torso remains upright and vertical with no lateral lean, the core appears engaged and tight, and the gaze is directed straight ahead at a fixed point.

exercises.name: Single Leg Calf Raise
exercises.pose_description: Standing on one leg with the other foot lifted off the ground, holding a wall or railing for balance. The heel of the standing foot rises as high as possible, pushing up onto the ball of the foot. The knee remains straight, the body stays tall, and the calf muscle fully contracts at the top.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands tall and upright on the ball of one foot with the heel lifted as high as possible, creating a straight vertical line from hip to the ball of the foot, while the opposite leg is lifted with the knee bent at approximately 90 degrees and held slightly out to the side for balance. The standing leg's knee remains fully extended and locked, the torso stays erect without leaning, and the calf muscle of the supporting leg appears fully contracted and defined. The hand lightly touches the wall or railing for stability as the body faces forward.

exercises.name: Single Leg Deadlift
exercises.pose_description: Standing on one leg with a slight bend in the standing knee. The torso hinges forward at the hips while the non-standing leg extends straight behind, creating a T shape with the body. The arms hang down or hold a weight, the back remains flat, and the hips stay squared to the floor. The movement is a controlled hip hinge with the hamstrings and glutes of the standing leg working eccentrically.
exercises.end_pose_description: The torso is nearly parallel to the ground in a deep hip hinge, with the standing leg's knee slightly bent and the non-standing leg extended straight back at hip height, forming a perfect horizontal line from the back leg through the torso. The back remains flat and rigid, the arms hang vertically downward (or hold a weight at the hips), and the standing leg's hamstrings and glutes appear fully engaged and tensioned. The person faces downward with their gaze following the neutral spine alignment.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Deadlifts with Dumbbells
exercises.pose_description: Stand on one leg holding a dumbbell in the opposite hand, maintaining a slight bend in your standing knee. Keep your chest up and engage your core for stability.
exercises.end_pose_description: Hinge at the hip while extending your free leg behind you for balance, lowering the dumbbell toward the ground. Return to standing by driving through your heel and squeezing your glute.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridges with Dumbbell
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with one knee bent and foot flat on the ground, the other leg extended straight up. Hold a dumbbell across your hips with both hands.
exercises.end_pose_description: Drive through your planted foot to lift your hips toward the ceiling, creating a straight line from knee to shoulders. Squeeze your glutes at the top before lowering back down.

exercises.name: Sleeper Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lying on the involved side with the shoulder and elbow each bent to 90 degrees, forearm pointing toward the ceiling. The opposite hand gently pushes the forearm of the bottom arm downward toward the floor, internally rotating the shoulder. The elbow remains at shoulder height and the body stays on its side without rolling backward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies on their side with the involved shoulder's forearm pressed down toward the floor in deep internal rotation, creating approximately a 45-50 degree angle between the forearm and the ground, while the opposite hand applies gentle pressure on top of the forearm. The elbow remains at shoulder height, the torso stays flat and aligned on its side without rolling backward, and the posterior shoulder and rotator cuff muscles appear visibly stretched and engaged.

exercises.name: Soleus Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing facing a wall with hands placed on the wall at shoulder height. One foot is positioned behind the other in a staggered stance. The back knee bends while keeping the heel on the floor, creating a stretch in the lower calf (soleus) of the back leg. The front knee is also slightly bent and the torso leans slightly forward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands in a deep forward lean against the wall with both hands pressed firmly at shoulder height, the back leg's knee deeply flexed (approximately 60-90 degrees) while the heel remains planted on the ground, and the front leg's knee bent at roughly 45 degrees to support the forward weight shift. The torso is angled forward noticeably from the hips, the soleus muscle of the back calf is visibly taut and stretched, and the person faces directly toward the wall with their body perpendicular to the ground.

exercises.name: Standing Adductor Stretch Against Wall
exercises.pose_description: Stand facing a wall or sturdy support with one hand on it for balance. Step your legs wide apart in a staggered stance.
exercises.end_pose_description: Shift your weight toward one leg, bending that knee while keeping the other leg straight. Feel the stretch along the inner thigh of the straight leg.

exercises.name: Standing Ankle Eversion with Band
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with a resistance band looped around both forefeet, with feet hip-width apart and knees slightly bent. Keep your core engaged for stability.
exercises.end_pose_description: Turn your feet outward (eversion) against the band resistance, actively engaging the peroneal muscles. Return to neutral position with control.

exercises.name: Standing Back Extension
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with feet hip-width apart and hands placed on the lower back for support. The torso gently leans backward, extending the lumbar spine while the hips push slightly forward. The head follows the natural curve of the spine, looking upward, and the knees remain straight. The movement is slow and controlled.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is arched backward at maximum extension with the torso creating a pronounced backward curve from the hips upward, chest lifted and thrust forward, head tilted back following the spinal curve, and both arms bent with hands pressing firmly against the lower back. The hips are thrust slightly forward as an anchor point, legs remain straight with knees locked, and the entire anterior chain (chest, abs, hip flexors) appears stretched and lengthened while the erector spinae muscles along the back are visibly engaged.

exercises.name: Standing Balance
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet hip-width apart next to a counter or wall for support, with fingertips lightly touching for safety. Distribute your weight evenly on both feet.
exercises.end_pose_description: Shift more weight onto the affected leg while maintaining light contact with the counter or wall. Hold for 20-30 seconds, building confidence and stability.

exercises.name: Standing Band Pallof Press
exercises.pose_description: Stand perpendicular to an anchor point with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent. Hold a looped band at chest height with both hands, band anchored at chest level beside you.
exercises.end_pose_description: Press the band straight out in front of your chest, fully extending your arms while resisting the rotational force. Return to chest height with control, engaging your core throughout.

exercises.name: Standing Band Pull-Apart
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent. Hold a resistance band at eye level with both hands, arms extended straight out in front of you.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull the band apart by moving your hands outward in an arc, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Return to the starting position with control, focusing on posterior chain engagement.

exercises.name: Standing Band Row
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and the resistance band looped under your feet. Hold both ends of the band with your arms extended straight down in front of you at hip level.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull the band up toward your ribcage by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together. Your elbows should move past your torso with the band handles coming toward your lower chest.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raises
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with feet hip-width apart, lightly holding a wall or chair for balance. Both heels are raised off the floor as high as possible by pushing up onto the balls of the feet, fully contracting the calf muscles. The body remains tall and straight with knees extended.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright on the balls of both feet with heels elevated several inches off the ground, ankles plantarflexed at maximum height, while knees remain fully extended and legs are straight. The calves are visibly contracted and bulging, the torso is vertical and stable, and the person lightly grips a wall or chair for balance with one or both hands.

exercises.name: Standing Chest Fly with Band
exercises.pose_description: Standing with a resistance band anchored behind at chest height, holding one end in each hand. Arms start extended out to the sides at shoulder height with a slight bend in the elbows. The arms sweep forward in an arc, bringing the hands together in front of the chest, squeezing the pectorals. The torso remains upright and stable.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with both arms bent at approximately 90 degrees, crossed in front of the chest with hands meeting near the centerline, elbows slightly lower than shoulder height. The chest muscles appear fully contracted and engaged, with the shoulders drawn slightly forward and the upper back rounded inward from the pectoral squeeze. The torso remains stable and vertical with no rotation.

exercises.name: Standing Dumbbell Reverse Fly
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding dumbbells at your sides with a slight bend in your elbows and knees. Hinge slightly at the hips while maintaining a neutral spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: Raise the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top. Lower the dumbbells back down in a controlled motion.

exercises.name: Standing Figure-Four Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright and place one hand on a wall or chair for balance. Cross the affected leg over the opposite thigh, creating a figure-four shape.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently lean forward, feeling a stretch in the outer hip and glute of the crossed leg. Maintain an upright chest and avoid rounding the spine.

exercises.name: Standing Hamstring Curl
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright holding onto a chair or counter for balance. One heel curls upward behind the body toward the buttock by bending the knee, engaging the hamstring. The thighs remain parallel, the standing leg is straight with a slight knee bend, and the torso stays upright without leaning forward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The exerciser stands upright facing forward with the standing leg nearly straight and slight knee bend, while the working leg is bent at approximately 90 degrees with the heel pulled up toward the glutes, creating a sharp knee angle. The hamstring of the bent leg appears visibly contracted and engaged, the torso remains perfectly vertical without any forward lean, and both hands maintain light contact with the chair/counter for balance.

exercises.name: Standing Heel Raises
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, hands resting on a wall or chair for balance. Keep your shoulders relaxed and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rise up onto the balls of your feet, lifting your heels off the ground as high as comfortable. Lower back down with control to the starting position.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Abduction
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright holding onto a chair or wall for balance with one hand. The outside leg lifts straight out to the side away from the body to approximately 30 to 45 degrees while keeping the toes pointed forward and the knee straight. The standing leg remains stable and the torso does not lean to the opposite side.
exercises.end_pose_description: Standing upright on the left leg. The right leg is lifted straight out to the side at approximately 45 degrees from the body. The right knee is straight and locked. Torso remains upright, not leaning.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Adduction
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with one foot firmly planted on the ground. Position the other leg straight and slightly out to the side, or directly alongside the standing leg, with the foot lightly touching the floor or hovering just above it, ready to initiate movement. Maintain an upright torso and a level pelvis, and you may hold onto a stable object for balance.
exercises.end_pose_description: The standing leg remains straight and planted while the working leg is fully crossed in front of the body at approximately 45 degrees, with the knee slightly bent, creating a diagonal line across the midline of the torso. The torso stays completely upright and facing forward with shoulders level and pelvis square, while the inner thigh and adductor muscles are visibly contracted as the leg reaches its furthest inward position.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Adduction with Dumbbell
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side, with feet hip-width apart. Hold onto a stable surface with your other hand for balance.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly bring the weighted leg across your body, adducting at the hip toward the midline. Control the weight as you return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Extension
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright holding a wall or chair for balance. One leg extends straight behind the body, squeezing the glute to drive the movement, while the knee remains straight. The torso stays upright and does not lean forward excessively. The leg lifts to approximately 15 to 20 degrees of hip extension.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with one leg extended straight behind the body at approximately 45 degrees of hip extension, knee fully straight, while the supporting leg remains vertical and locked. The torso remains perpendicular to the ground with no forward lean, and the glute of the extended leg appears visibly contracted and engaged. The arms maintain contact with the wall or chair for balance.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Flexion
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright holding a wall or chair for balance. One knee lifts forward and upward in front of the body, bringing the thigh toward the chest until the hip reaches approximately 90 degrees of flexion. The knee is bent, the standing leg remains straight, and the torso stays tall without leaning backward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The standing figure faces forward with the torso upright and vertical, one leg extended straight down to support the body while the other knee is raised high in front, with the thigh parallel to the ground at approximately 90 degrees hip flexion and the knee bent at roughly 90 degrees. The lifted leg's hip flexors and quadriceps appear visibly engaged, the standing leg's quadriceps and glutes are tensed to maintain stability, and the core appears braced to keep the torso from leaning backward.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Flexor and Quad Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing on one leg, the other foot pulled behind toward the glutes with one hand gripping the ankle. The standing leg is slightly bent. Free arm extended to the side for balance. Hips pushed slightly forward to emphasize the hip flexor and quad stretch. Relaxed posture suggesting an evening cooldown.
exercises.end_pose_description: The standing leg remains slightly bent while the stretched leg is pulled up behind the body with the knee deeply flexed (approximately 90 degrees), foot drawn close to the glutes with the hand firmly gripping the ankle. The torso is upright with a slight forward pelvic tilt, the free arm extended out to the side for balance, and the person faces forward with a relaxed, neutral expression. The hip flexors and quadriceps of the back leg appear fully lengthened and engaged in the stretch.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Flexor March
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, maintaining good posture and a slight bend in your knees. You may hold onto a chair or wall for balance if needed.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly lift one knee up toward your chest in a controlled manner, then lower it back down. Alternate legs in a slow, deliberate marching motion to improve hip mobility.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Internal Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright on one leg with knee bent to 90 degrees, holding onto a support for balance. Keep your standing leg slightly bent and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your lifted leg outward at the hip, moving your foot away from your body in a semicircular motion. Return to center in a controlled manner and repeat.

exercises.name: Standing Marching in Place
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with good posture, feet hip-width apart, and arms at your sides or ready to swing. Look straight ahead.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lift one knee up to hip height while swinging the opposite arm forward in a marching motion. Alternate legs in a controlled, rhythmic pattern.

exercises.name: Standing Marching
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, arms at your sides, and good posture throughout. Keep your core engaged and look straight ahead.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly lift one knee up in a marching motion while maintaining balance and posture. Alternate legs in a controlled pace, swinging arms naturally as if marching in place.

exercises.name: Standing Pelvic Tilts
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees slightly bent. Place hands on your lower abdomen or lower back for feedback.
exercises.end_pose_description: Tilt your pelvis by tightening your core and rotating your pelvis upward, flattening the natural curve of your lower back. Return to neutral and repeat.

exercises.name: Standing Posterior Shoulder Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides. Use your unaffected hand to gently grasp your affected arm just above the elbow.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull your affected arm across your body toward your opposite shoulder, feeling a gentle stretch in the posterior shoulder and rotator cuff. Hold this stretch without bouncing for 20-30 seconds.

exercises.name: Standing Quad Sets Against Wall
exercises.pose_description: Stand with your back against a wall and your feet hip-width apart, positioned about 12 inches away from the wall. Keep your hands resting on your thighs.
exercises.end_pose_description: Tighten the quadriceps muscle on top of your thigh by straightening your knee fully and pushing it back slightly into the wall. Hold the muscle contraction for 2-3 seconds, then relax.

exercises.name: Standing Quad Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright and tall, facing the camera, balancing on one leg. Use one hand to hold a wall or sturdy object for support. Bend the knee of the free leg and grasp its ankle or top of the foot with the same-side hand, bringing the heel close to the glutes with both knees near each other.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright on one straight leg while the opposite leg is bent at approximately 90 degrees with the heel pulled close to or touching the buttock, creating a vertical line from hip to knee. The same-side arm reaches back to grasp the foot/ankle, pulling it upward, while the supporting arm remains lightly on the wall or chair for balance. The torso is upright and squared forward, the pelvis is level and slightly tucked, and the quadriceps of the bent leg appear visibly stretched and engaged.

exercises.name: Standing Rotation with Band
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and a resistance band secured at chest height in front of you, holding both ends with arms extended. Keep your hips still and facing forward throughout the exercise.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your torso and arms to one side against the band resistance, keeping your core engaged and lower back stable. Return to center with control and repeat on the opposite side.

exercises.name: Standing Row with Band
exercises.pose_description: Stand facing a resistance band anchored directly in front of you at chest height. Grip the band handles with both hands, arms fully extended forward at shoulder height, feeling tension in the band. Maintain a tall, upright posture with feet parallel or staggered for stability.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees, pulled tight against the ribcage with hands drawn back toward the lower chest/upper abdomen. The shoulder blades are visibly retracted and squeezed together, creating prominent definition across the upper back and rear shoulders, while the chest is slightly puffed forward. The resistance band is maximally stretched with tension visible in the biceps and upper back musculature.

exercises.name: Standing Single-Leg Balance
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, hands resting on a wall or sturdy chair. Keep your core engaged and eyes focused on a fixed point.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lift one foot off the ground, balancing on the other leg while maintaining an upright posture. Hold the position for 10-30 seconds, using the chair for light support as needed.

exercises.name: Standing Single-Leg Balance with Hip Stability
exercises.target_area: Hip stabilizers, gluteus medius, proprioception, lower back
exercises.pose_description: Standing on one leg with the standing knee slightly bent, focusing on keeping the pelvis level without dropping on the unsupported side. The non-standing leg is lifted with the knee bent to approximately 90 degrees of hip flexion. Arms are at sides or on hips, the torso is tall, and the gluteus medius of the standing leg is actively engaged to maintain pelvic stability.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands tall on one leg with a slightly bent knee, maintaining a perfectly level pelvis without any lateral drop, while the opposite leg remains lifted with the knee bent at approximately 90 degrees of hip flexion and positioned in front of the body. The torso is upright and centered over the standing leg's foot, with visible tension through the glutes and hip stabilizers of the standing side, while the arms are either relaxed at the sides or resting on the hips, and the gaze is fixed forward.

exercises.name: Standing Single-Leg Calf Raises
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright on one leg with your hands lightly touching a wall or rail for balance. Keep your core engaged and your standing leg slightly bent.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rise up onto the ball of your foot, lifting your heel off the ground as high as possible. Lower back down with control and repeat on the same leg before switching sides.

exercises.name: Standing Spinal Extension
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and hands placed on your lower back for support. Engage your core and maintain good posture throughout the movement.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently arch backward by extending your spine, using your hands for light support and balance. Move only as far as comfortable without causing pain or dizziness.

exercises.name: Standing Thoracic Extension
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and place hands clasped behind your head with elbows pointing outward. Engage your core and maintain a neutral spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently arch backward from the thoracic spine while keeping your lower back stable and core engaged. Look slightly upward without overextending your neck.

exercises.name: Standing Wall Marching
exercises.pose_description: Stand facing a wall at arm's length distance with your hands resting lightly on the wall for balance. Keep your feet hip-width apart and your posture upright.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly lift one knee up toward your chest in a controlled marching motion, then lower it back down. Alternate legs in a steady, controlled manner while maintaining contact with the wall for support.

exercises.name: Standing Wall Push-Off
exercises.pose_description: Stand facing a wall at arm's length away with your hands placed on the wall at shoulder height, shoulder-width apart. Keep your body straight and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Bend your elbows to bring your chest closer to the wall, then push through your hands to return to the starting position. This modified push-up maintains shoulder stability while building strength.

exercises.name: Standing Wall Push-Ups
exercises.pose_description: Stand facing a wall at arm's length distance with your feet hip-width apart and hands placed on the wall at shoulder height. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
exercises.end_pose_description: Bend your elbows and lean your body toward the wall in a controlled manner, then push back to the starting position. This modified push-up builds upper body and core strength with reduced ankle stress.

exercises.name: Stationary Bike
exercises.pose_description: Sit on the stationary bike seat with your back upright and hands on the handlebars. Adjust the seat height so your knee has a slight bend at the bottom of each pedal stroke.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pedal smoothly at a moderate pace with controlled movements, maintaining an upright posture. Focus on smooth, pain-free circular motions through the full range available.

exercises.name: Step-Ups
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright facing a low step or platform approximately 6 to 8 inches high. One foot is placed entirely on the step, and the body is driven upward by pressing through that foot until standing tall on the step with both feet. Arms may be at sides or held at the waist for balance.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands fully upright on the elevated step platform with both feet planted side-by-side, knees extended and legs straight, torso erect and shoulders back. The quadriceps, glutes, and calf muscles are visibly engaged and contracted, with the entire body weight supported on the elevated surface. Arms are positioned at the sides or waist for balance, and the person faces forward in a stable, neutral standing position.

exercises.name: Straight Leg Raises
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with one knee bent and foot flat on the floor for support. The other leg is lifted straight off the ground to approximately 45 degrees with the knee fully locked and toes pointed toward the ceiling. Arms rest at sides, and the lower back maintains contact with the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lying flat on the back on the ground, face up. The left knee is bent with foot flat on the floor. The right leg is raised straight up to approximately 45 degrees from the floor with the knee fully locked.

exercises.name: Superman Exercise
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down with arms extended overhead on the floor and legs straight behind. Both arms and both legs simultaneously lift off the floor, arching the back and engaging the erector spinae and glutes. The head lifts with the chest and the gaze is directed at the floor. The position is held briefly at the top with the body forming a shallow U shape.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies prone with arms fully extended overhead and legs straight, both lifted several inches off the ground, creating a shallow U-shaped arch through the torso. The chest, arms, and thighs are elevated while the pelvis remains as the lowest point, with the head held neutral and gaze directed downward. The erector spinae along the spine and glute muscles are visibly contracted, creating definition along the back and posterior chain.

exercises.name: Supine Achilles Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with both legs extended on the floor. Use a towel or resistance band looped around the ball of one foot.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently pull the towel or band toward your body, flexing your foot to stretch the calf and Achilles tendon. Keep your leg straight and hold the stretch without bouncing.

exercises.name: Supine Adductor Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Position your feet hip-width apart with arms at your sides.
exercises.end_pose_description: Drop one knee outward to the side while keeping the other foot planted, feeling a gentle stretch along the inner thigh. Hold this position with controlled breathing.

exercises.name: Supine Gentle Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Bring one arm across your chest towards the opposite shoulder, with the elbow bent. Use your other hand to gently hold the elbow of the arm being stretched.
exercises.end_pose_description: Using your unaffected hand, gently pull your affected arm across your body toward the opposite side, creating a mild stretch in the posterior shoulder. Hold this comfortable stretch for 20-30 seconds without forcing beyond a gentle sensation.

exercises.name: Supine External Rotation with Bent Elbow
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with your affected shoulder abducted to 90 degrees and elbow bent to 90 degrees, so your forearm points toward the ceiling. Keep your elbow in contact with the floor throughout the movement.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly rotate your forearm toward the floor in an external rotation movement, moving only as far as comfort allows without forcing the range. Hold for 1-2 seconds at the end range, then return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Supine External Rotation with Dumbbell
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with your affected shoulder abducted to 90 degrees and elbow bent to 90 degrees. Hold a light dumbbell in your hand with your forearm perpendicular to your body.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your forearm upward toward the floor above your head, moving only at the shoulder's external rotators. Keep your elbow fixed at 90 degrees and stop at a comfortable range without pain.

exercises.name: Supine Figure-4 Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Cross your right ankle over your left thigh just above the knee.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently pull your left thigh toward your chest, keeping your head and shoulders relaxed on the ground. Feel the stretch in your right hip and external rotators.

exercises.name: Supine Figure-4 Stretch with Pelvic Mobilization
exercises.target_area: Piriformis, gluteal muscles, hip external rotators
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with one ankle crossed over the opposite knee in a figure-four position. Both hands reach through and clasp behind the thigh of the bottom leg, pulling it toward the chest. Additionally, the pelvis gently rocks side to side in small mobilization movements, enhancing the stretch through the piriformis and outer hip of the crossed leg.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine on their back with the left ankle crossed over the right knee in a tight figure-4 position, while both hands clasp firmly behind the right thigh, pulling it toward the chest with the right knee bent at approximately 90 degrees and drawn close to the torso. The pelvis is tilted at its maximum lateral rotation point (either left or right side slightly lifted), creating a deep stretch visible through the tensed piriformis and glute muscles of the crossed leg, with the head and shoulders remaining flat against the ground.

exercises.name: Supine Figure Four Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Cross your right ankle over your left knee to form a figure-four shape.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull your left knee toward your chest, allowing the stretch to deepen in your right hip and glute. Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.

exercises.name: Supine Glute Bridge
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, positioned hip-width apart and close to your buttocks. Place arms at your sides with palms down.
exercises.end_pose_description: Press through your heels and lift your hips toward the ceiling, creating a straight line from knees to shoulders. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower with control.

exercises.name: Supine Hamstring Curls
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Keep the affected leg in a comfortable position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slide the heel of the affected leg toward the buttock, bending the knee fully while keeping the foot on the floor. Return to starting position.

exercises.name: Supine Hamstring Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with one leg extended on the floor. The other leg is raised straight up toward the ceiling with the knee as straight as possible, hands clasped behind the thigh or a strap looped around the foot to assist the stretch. The hips remain flat on the floor and the lower back maintains a neutral position.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies flat on their back with one leg fully extended along the floor and the other leg raised nearly perpendicular to the body (90+ degrees at the hip), knee straight or nearly straight, with hands clasped behind the thigh or a strap around the foot pulling gently toward the torso. The hamstring of the raised leg appears visibly contracted and engaged, the hips remain square and flat against the floor, and the lower back maintains contact with the ground with the head neutral or slightly forward.

exercises.name: Supine Hip Abduction
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Keep your arms at your sides for stability.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly slide one foot outward along the floor, abducting the hip while keeping the knee bent. Return to the starting position and repeat on both sides.

exercises.name: Supine Hip Bridges
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, and arms at your sides. Keep the affected leg in a comfortable, supported position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Press through your heels to lift your hips toward the ceiling, creating a straight line from knees to shoulders. Hold briefly and lower back down.

exercises.name: Supine Hip External Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, roughly hip-width apart. Your arms should rest comfortably at your sides, palms facing down.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies flat on their back with the left knee bent approximately 90 degrees and dropped maximally outward toward the floor, with the left foot remaining planted and the lower leg externally rotated, while the right leg stays stationary with knee bent and foot flat. The pelvis remains level and neutral, the torso stays flat against the ground, and the glutes and hip external rotators of the working leg appear engaged and stretched at end-range.

exercises.name: Supine Hip Flexion
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with both legs extended. One knee bends and lifts toward the chest, driven by the hip flexors, bringing the thigh to approximately 90 degrees of hip flexion. The opposite leg remains flat on the floor, the lower back stays neutral, and the hands may gently guide the knee.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies flat on their back with one knee bent and drawn up toward the chest at approximately 90 degrees of hip flexion, while the opposite leg remains fully extended and flat on the floor. The hip flexors and iliopsoas are visibly engaged as the bent knee approaches the torso, the lower back maintains contact with the floor, and the hands gently cradle the lifted knee. The head and shoulders remain relaxed against the ground, facing upward.

exercises.name: Supine Hip Internal Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, positioned wider than hip-width apart.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine with their right knee dropped maximally inward toward the left side of their body, creating an acute angle at the hip while the right foot remains planted on the floor, and the left leg stays stationary with knee bent at approximately 90 degrees. The pelvis remains level against the floor, the torso stays flat and centered, and the internal rotators of the right hip appear engaged and stretched as the knee points toward the midline.
