exercises.pose_description: Sit upright holding a light dumbbell with both hands, raising it overhead with elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees. Your elbows should stay close to your head and relatively stationary.
exercises.end_pose_description: Sit upright, holding the dumbbell overhead with both hands. Both arms are fully extended straight up towards the ceiling, with the elbows completely straightened and still close to your head. The triceps are visibly engaged.

exercises.name: Passive Elbow Flexion Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with your right arm extended straight out in front of you at shoulder height, palm facing down. Use your left hand to gently grasp your right wrist or forearm.
exercises.end_pose_description: Sit upright with your right elbow deeply bent, bringing your right hand close to your right shoulder, with the palm still facing generally downwards. Your left hand firmly grasps your right wrist or forearm, actively pulling to deepen the stretch on the triceps brachii muscle along the back of your right upper arm.

exercises.name: Wrist Flexion with Dumbbell
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your forearm resting on your thigh, palm facing up, holding a light dumbbell in your hand with your wrist in a neutral position. Keep your forearm stable and in contact with your leg.
exercises.end_pose_description: Sit with your forearm still resting on your thigh, palm facing up, holding the light dumbbell, your wrist fully flexed so the dumbbell is positioned as close as possible to your forearm. The muscles on the underside of your forearm are visibly contracted, while the muscles on the top of your forearm are elongated.

exercises.name: Elbow Flexion Stretch with Towel
exercises.pose_description: Stand with your right arm raised overhead and bent at the elbow, so your hand drops behind your back. Relax your shoulders and maintain an upright posture.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your right elbow is acutely bent, with your right hand positioned significantly lower down your upper back. Your left arm is raised overhead, with your left hand gripping a towel that is also held by your right hand, creating a gentle downward tension on your right arm. The triceps muscle on the back of your right arm is elongated, with your shoulders relaxed and posture upright.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding light dumbbells in each hand with arms at your sides and palms facing your thighs (neutral grip). Keep your elbows stationary close to your body.
exercises.end_pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding light dumbbells in each hand. Your forearms are vertical, and the dumbbells are positioned close to your shoulders, with palms still facing each other. Elbows remain stationary and tucked close to the body. The biceps and brachioradialis muscles are visibly contracted, and the triceps are stretched.

exercises.name: Standing Balance on One Leg
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with your hand on a wall or rail for light support if needed. Both feet are on the ground, shoulder-width apart.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body is upright, balanced on one straight leg with the foot of the other leg lifted several inches off the ground, knee slightly bent. The gluteus medius, quadriceps, and calf of the standing leg are visibly engaged, and hands maintain light contact with the wall or rail if needed for stability.

exercises.name: Prone Knee Flexion with Band
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on the floor with a resistance band looped around your foot. Your arms are folded under your forehead for support.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lie face down on the floor, with your arms folded under your forehead, and one leg straight. The other knee is maximally bent, bringing that foot's heel as close as possible to the glutes. The resistance band around the working foot is taut, highlighting strongly contracted hamstrings and visibly stretched quadriceps.

exercises.name: Supine Hip Abduction with Band
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat on the floor. A resistance band is looped around both knees.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies on their back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. The resistance band is taut and stretched, holding both knees as far apart as possible. The outer hip and gluteal muscles are visibly contracted, while the inner thigh muscles appear stretched.

exercises.name: Seated Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright on the edge of a sturdy chair with both feet flat on the floor. Your surgical leg is positioned on the chair.
exercises.end_pose_description: The torso is leaned backward from the hips, maintaining an upright upper body, while the non-surgical foot remains flat on the floor. Your surgical leg's hip is deeply extended, causing a visible stretch across the front of the hip joint where the hip flexor muscles are lengthened.

exercises.name: Standing Balance on One Leg
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with your hand on a wall or counter for light support. Your weight is evenly distributed on both feet.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your body is upright, with your hand resting lightly on the wall or counter. All your weight rests on one foot, with the other foot lifted a few inches from the floor and its knee gently bent. The muscles of the standing leg and your core are visibly engaged to maintain balance.

exercises.name: Supine Isometric Shoulder Hold
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with the repaired arm positioned at 45 degrees away from your body, elbow slightly bent. Your forearm points upward toward the ceiling.
exercises.end_pose_description: The repaired arm remains positioned at 45 degrees away from your body, with the elbow slightly bent, and the forearm pointing upward toward the ceiling. The anterior and medial deltoid muscles are visibly contracted, maintaining this static arm position.

exercises.name: Supine Shoulder Abduction Slide
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with both arms at your sides, palms facing down on the surface. Your shoulders are relaxed and in neutral alignment.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your arms are extended out to your sides, forming a 'T' shape with your body, with palms remaining on the surface and facing down. Your shoulders are still relaxed and pressed gently into the surface. The middle deltoids and supraspinatus are visibly engaged.

exercises.name: Seated Shoulder Flexion with Support
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a firm chair with both arms resting on your thighs. Your spine is straight and your core is gently engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: One arm is raised directly forward and upward, with the elbow straight, reaching towards the ceiling. Your other hand gently supports the wrist of the raised arm, assisting its elevation. Your spine remains straight, your core gently engaged, and the anterior deltoid and rotator cuff muscles of the raised shoulder are contracted.

exercises.name: Standing Postural Alignment
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms hanging naturally at your sides. Notice your current shoulder position and posture.
exercises.end_pose_description: The shoulders are gently pulled back and down, away from the ears, with the chest open and lifted. The shoulder blades are subtly retracted, and the arms remain hanging naturally at the sides in an upright and aligned posture. The rhomboids and lower trapezius muscles are engaged, while the pectorals feel a gentle stretch.

exercises.name: Supine Chest Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with your repaired arm positioned out to the side at 90 degrees, elbow slightly bent. Your uninvolved arm rests across your body.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your trunk is gently rotated away from your repaired arm, with your head turned in the same direction, causing your repaired shoulder and chest to visibly stretch. The pectoralis major and anterior deltoid muscles are elongated in this peak stretch. Your repaired arm maintains its 90-degree abduction and slightly bent elbow from the starting position, while your uninvolved arm rests across your body.

exercises.name: Seated Elbow Flexion Active Assist
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with your repaired arm resting on your lap, elbow extended. Your uninvolved arm is positioned nearby to provide assistance.
exercises.end_pose_description: Sit upright with your repaired arm's elbow fully flexed, its hand positioned near your shoulder. The forearm is held vertically, perpendicular to the upper arm. Your uninvolved hand cradles the wrist of the repaired arm, supporting it in this peak position. The biceps brachii is visibly contracted, and the triceps brachii is stretched.

exercises.name: Supine Prone Walk
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with both arms at your sides, legs extended. Your core is gently engaged and your spine maintains neutral alignment.
exercises.end_pose_description: Both arms are fully extended overhead with elbows straight, hands positioned directly above the head, palms facing each other. Your shoulders are in full flexion, biceps aligned near the ears, and your shoulder blades are upwardly rotated and elevated. The deltoids, serratus anterior, and upper trapezius are visibly engaged, while the latissimus dorsi and pectoralis major are stretched. Your core remains gently engaged, and legs extended, maintaining neutral spine alignment.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Deadlifts (Light)
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet hip-width apart holding light dumbbells at your sides with arms straight. Keep your chest up and shoulders back.
exercises.end_pose_description: Torso is hinged forward at the hips, nearly parallel to the floor, with a slight bend in the knees. The dumbbells hang straight down, near the shins, while the back remains flat and straight. Hamstrings and glutes are visibly stretched, and the lower back muscles are engaged to maintain spinal alignment.

exercises.name: Supine Knee Flexion
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with both legs extended on the floor or a bed. Keep your pelvis neutral and relaxed.
exercises.end_pose_description: One knee is bent, with the sole of that foot flat on the floor or bed, positioned close to the buttocks. The thigh of this leg is angled upwards towards the chest, while the opposing leg remains extended. The pelvis stays neutral and relaxed, with the hamstrings visibly engaged and the front of the hip gently stretched.

exercises.name: Supine Hip Abduction with Band
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Place a resistance band around both thighs just above the knees.
exercises.end_pose_description: The individual is on their back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, now significantly wider than hip-width apart. The knees are widely separated, pushing outward against the taut resistance band around the thighs. The gluteus medius and minimus are visibly contracted.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Flexion with Band
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright facing a stable surface for light support, with a resistance band looped around one foot. Keep your standing leg straight with a slight knee bend for stability.
exercises.end_pose_description: Maintain an upright posture, still facing the stable surface, with the resistance band looped around one foot. The banded leg is positioned with the thigh roughly parallel to the floor and the knee bent at approximately 90 degrees. The standing leg remains straight with a slight knee bend for stability, and the hip flexors of the raised leg are visibly engaged.

exercises.name: Supine Hip Internal/External Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with one hip and knee bent to 90 degrees, with a light resistance band around the thigh. Keep your lower back neutral and engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: The bent hip is fully externally rotated, with the knee remaining at 90 degrees. The lower leg and foot are positioned laterally away from the body's midline, reaching the maximum comfortable range. The gluteal muscles and deep hip rotators are engaged, and the hip adductors and internal rotators are stretched, with the lower back still neutral and engaged.

exercises.name: Supine Hip Adduction with Band
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart. Place a resistance band around both thighs above the knees.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Both knees are pressed firmly together, actively squeezing against the resistance band. The inner thigh and adductor muscles are visibly engaged and contracted.

exercises.name: Sidelying Hip Abduction with Band
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your side with legs extended and stacked, with a resistance band looped around both legs just above the knees. Keep your core engaged and head resting on your arm.
exercises.end_pose_description: The bottom leg remains extended and rested on the floor, while the top leg is extended and elevated directly upwards, away from the bottom leg, as far as possible without tilting the torso. The resistance band above the knees is taut, and the gluteus medius on the top leg is visibly engaged. The core is engaged, and the head rests on the arm.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Extension with Band
exercises.pose_description: Stand facing a stable surface with a resistance band looped around one foot, keeping your posture upright. Engage your core and hold the support surface lightly.
exercises.end_pose_description: The banded leg is extended directly backward, with the foot elevated slightly behind the body. The supporting leg remains straight, and the torso stays upright with the core engaged, maintaining a light hold on the support surface. The glutes and hamstrings of the extended leg are contracted, with the hip flexors on that same side elongated.

exercises.name: Figure-4 Stretch with Band Assist
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with one knee bent and crossed over the opposite thigh in a figure-4 position. Place a band around the thigh of the bottom leg for gentle assistance.
exercises.end_pose_description: The bottom knee is positioned close to the chest, with the band taut around its thigh. The hands grasp the band, maintaining a significant stretch through the outer hip and gluteal muscles of the crossed leg.

exercises.name: Supine Shoulder Shrugs
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, arms at your sides with palms facing down. Your shoulders are relaxed and in neutral position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, arms at your sides with palms facing down. Your shoulders are elevated, drawn upwards towards your ears, creating maximum separation from the ribcage. The upper trapezius muscles are visibly contracted.

exercises.name: Supine Elbow Flexion with Arm Support
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent and the affected arm resting at your side with elbow extended. Place a small pillow under the affected arm for support.
exercises.end_pose_description: The individual remains on their back with knees bent. The affected arm continues to be supported by the pillow, with the elbow fully flexed and the hand positioned near the shoulder. The biceps brachii and brachialis muscles are visibly contracted.

exercises.name: Standing Wall Slides
exercises.pose_description: Stand with your back against a wall, feet 6 inches away from the wall, and arms at shoulder height with elbows bent 90 degrees. Your forearms are parallel to the ground.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your back and feet remain in the same position against the wall. Your arms are fully extended directly overhead, with your elbows straight, and the back of your hands, forearms, and upper arms pressed firmly against the wall. The serratus anterior and trapezius are visibly engaged, while the pectoralis major and latissimus dorsi are stretched.

exercises.name: Seated Torso Rotations
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with feet flat on the floor and hands crossed loosely over your chest. Your hips remain stable and facing forward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The upper body is positioned facing to one side, with the shoulders, chest, and head oriented in that direction. The hands remain crossed over the chest, aligned with the torso's current alignment. The abdominal obliques on the side of the torso's turned position are visibly contracted, and the opposing obliques and spinal rotators are elongated.

exercises.name: Lying Affected Side Rotation with Pillow
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your unaffected side with hips and knees slightly bent for stability, and place a pillow between your knees. Your affected arm is bent at the elbow and rests on your torso.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your unaffected side remains stable, with hips and knees bent and the pillow still secured between them. Your affected elbow stays bent at 90 degrees, fixed against your torso, while your forearm is externally rotated until the back of your hand points towards the surface behind your head. The posterior rotator cuff muscles are engaged, and the anterior shoulder muscles are visibly stretched.

exercises.name: Seated Chin Tucks
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with good posture, eyes looking straight ahead, and shoulders relaxed. Your spine is neutral and supported against the chair back.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your head is retracted straight back, creating a visible double chin, with your eyes still looking straight ahead. The back of your neck appears elongated, and the muscles at the base of your skull are visibly stretched. Your shoulders remain relaxed, and your spine is neutral and supported against the chair back.

exercises.name: Cervical Isometric Holds
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with shoulders relaxed and spine neutral. Place your hand gently against the side of your head at temple level.
exercises.end_pose_description: The upright seated posture is maintained with shoulders relaxed and spine neutral. Your hand remains against your temple, and your head applies firm pressure into your hand, maintaining a neutral neck position. The sternocleidomastoid and scalene muscles on the side where your hand rests are visibly engaged.

exercises.name: Scapular Squeeze with Dumbbells
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright holding light dumbbells at your sides with arms extended and palms facing inward. Keep your neck in a neutral position with minimal movement.
exercises.end_pose_description: The shoulders are pulled back, with the shoulder blades maximally squeezed towards the spine, causing the chest to visibly expand. Dumbbells remain at your sides with arms extended, palms facing inward, and positioned slightly further back, while the rhomboids and middle trapezius muscles of the upper back are visibly contracted and the neck remains neutral.

exercises.name: Supine Dumbbell Chest Press
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, and dumbbells held at chest level with elbows at 90 degrees. Ensure your head and neck remain supported and neutral.
exercises.end_pose_description: Maintain your back on the mat, knees bent, and feet flat, with dumbbells held directly above the center of the chest and arms fully extended upwards, ensuring a very slight bend at the elbows. The chest muscles (pectorals) are visibly contracted, and your head and neck remain supported and neutral.

exercises.name: Supine Bridge
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, and arms at your sides. Keep your neck relaxed and head supported by the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: The hips are lifted high off the floor, forming a straight diagonal line from the knees to the shoulders. The glutes, hamstrings, and lower back muscles are visibly contracted and engaged, holding this elevated position. The upper back, shoulders, and head remain on the floor, and the feet are flat.

exercises.name: Gentle Finger Flexion Exercises
exercises.pose_description: Sit comfortably with your forearm supported on a table, palm facing down. Keep your wrist in a neutral position with fingers fully extended.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your forearm remains supported on the table with the palm facing down and the wrist in a neutral position. The fingers are gently curled towards the palm, with the finger flexor muscles in the forearm gently engaged. A mild stretch is visible along the back of the hand.

exercises.name: Supination and Pronation
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your elbow bent at 90 degrees, tucked against your side, holding a light weight or object in your hand. Start with your palm facing down.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your elbow remains bent at 90 degrees and tucked against your side, holding the light weight or object in your hand. Your palm is facing directly upward. The supinator and biceps brachii muscles are visibly engaged in the forearm and upper arm, while the pronator muscles are stretched.

exercises.name: Scar Tissue Mobilization
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your forearm supported on a table, gently exposing the surgical incision site on your wrist or palm. Use your opposite hand to apply light pressure.
exercises.end_pose_description: The opposite hand maintains light pressure, gently stretching the skin and underlying tissue around the incision site in one direction. This action creates a visible tautness across the scar, while the wrist is held in a position of slight flexion or extension to facilitate the stretch. The superficial muscles and fascia around the scar appear gently elongated.

exercises.name: Active Wrist Radial Deviation
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your forearm resting on a table in a neutral position, palm facing downward. Keep your hand relaxed with fingers extended.
exercises.end_pose_description: The forearm remains resting on the table with the palm still facing downward. The hand is angled upwards at the wrist, with the thumb side elevated as far as possible towards the forearm. The fingers remain extended, and the muscles on the radial (thumb) side of the forearm are visibly engaged, while the ulnar (pinky) side of the wrist is visibly stretched.

exercises.name: Towel Grip and Release
exercises.pose_description: Sit with a rolled towel on a table in front of you. Place your open hand flat on top of the towel with fingers extended and relaxed.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your fingers are tightly curled around the rolled towel, compressing it firmly within your palm. The thumb is adducted and flexed, pressing into the towel from the opposite side. Intrinsic hand muscles and forearm flexors are visibly engaged in a strong grip.

exercises.name: Thumb Opposition Exercise
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your hand resting on a table, palm facing upward with all fingers extended. Keep your wrist in a neutral position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your hand remains resting on the table, palm facing upward, with your wrist in a neutral position. The tip of your thumb is pressed against the tip of your pinky finger. Your index, middle, and ring fingers remain extended, and the thenar eminence muscles at the base of your thumb are visibly engaged.

exercises.name: Seated Ankle Plantarflexion with Band
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with your legs extended in front of you. Loop a resistance band around the ball of your foot with your heel resting on the ground.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your foot is pointed downwards, pressing the ball of your foot into the resistance band. Your heel remains resting on the ground, with your calf muscles visibly contracted. The muscles on the front of your shin are in a lengthened position.

exercises.name: Supine Ankle Dorsiflexion with Band
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with legs extended and a resistance band looped around the ball of your foot. Keep your heel on the surface with your foot in a neutral position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your legs remain extended with the heel still on the surface. The top of your foot is positioned as close to your shin as possible, with the toes pointing upwards towards your head. The tibialis anterior muscle on the front of your shin is taut, and the calf muscles are stretched.

exercises.name: Supine Gluteal Bridge
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, positioned hip-width apart and arms at your sides. Position feet approximately 12 inches from your buttocks.
exercises.end_pose_description: The hips are elevated off the floor, creating a straight line from the shoulders through the hips to the knees. The knees remain bent with feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, and arms stay at the sides. The gluteal muscles are maximally contracted, and the hamstrings are engaged, with a visible stretch through the front of the hips.

exercises.name: Standing Quad Sets with Band
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with a resistance band looped around your knee and the other end anchored low behind you. Keep your knee slightly bent and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Stand upright with your knee fully extended, holding the resistance band taut and stretched behind it. Your quadriceps are intensely contracted and visibly tensed, maintaining the forward position of the knee against the band's pull. Your core remains engaged.

exercises.name: Standing Supported Marching
exercises.pose_description: Stand facing a wall or sturdy surface with both hands lightly supporting yourself. Distribute your weight evenly on both feet with good posture.
exercises.end_pose_description: Both hands remain lightly on the wall or sturdy surface. Your left foot is lifted off the floor, with the left hip and knee flexed so the left thigh is parallel to the floor. Your entire body weight rests on your straight right leg, with noticeable tension in the right calf and gluteal muscles. The core is engaged to maintain an upright, stable torso.

exercises.name: Prone Hip Extension with Band
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on a comfortable surface with a resistance band looped around both feet. Rest your forehead on your arms to maintain neutral spine alignment.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your legs are straight and slightly elevated a few inches off the surface, with the resistance band under tension around your feet. Your gluteal muscles are visibly contracted, indicating hip extension, while your forehead remains resting on your arms with a neutral spine alignment.

exercises.name: Seated Hamstring Stretch with Band
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with one leg extended in front of you and the other knee bent with foot on the floor. Place a resistance band around the ball of your extended foot, holding both ends.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your torso is leaned forward from the hips, positioned closely to the extended leg while maintaining a straight back. Your hands hold the resistance band taut, creating visible tension as the hamstring of the extended leg is stretched.

exercises.name: Prone Hamstring Isometric Hold
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on a firm surface with legs extended straight behind you. Place your forehead on your hands for comfort and support.
exercises.end_pose_description: Maintain the prone position with your forehead resting on your hands. One leg remains extended straight behind you, while the other leg is bent at the knee so the heel points directly towards the ceiling. The knee of the bent leg forms approximately a 90-degree angle. The hamstrings of the bent leg are visibly flexed and contracted, holding the lower leg elevated against gravity.

exercises.name: Supine Bridge Hold
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor hip-width apart. Arms are at your sides with palms down.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your hips are elevated off the floor so that a straight line extends from your shoulders through your hips to your knees. Your feet remain flat on the floor, hip-width apart, with knees bent. Your arms are at your sides with palms down. Hamstrings and glutes are engaged.

exercises.name: Seated Forward Fold
exercises.pose_description: Sit on the floor with both legs extended in front of you. Keep your spine tall and shoulders relaxed.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your torso is folded over your thighs, with your arms reaching towards your feet or holding your ankles/toes. Your head is relaxed towards your knees, and your spine is gently rounded. Your hamstrings are visibly elongated and deeply stretched.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Hinge
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips. Engage your core and maintain a neutral spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your torso is hinged forward from the hips, nearly parallel to the floor, with your hips pushed prominently backward; your knees maintain a soft bend, and your core remains engaged, preserving a neutral spine. The hamstrings are visibly lengthened, and the glutes are stretched.

exercises.name: Supine Glute Activation
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, positioned directly under your knees. Arms are at your sides.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your hips are elevated off the floor, forming a straight line from your shoulders to your knees. Your feet remain flat on the floor with knees bent, and arms are at your sides. Your glutes are visibly contracted, hamstrings are engaged, and the core is firm.

exercises.name: Quadruped Leg Lift
exercises.pose_description: Start on your hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips. Keep your spine neutral and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: One knee remains under its hip, with the hands under the shoulders. The other leg is elevated behind the body, its knee bent at 90 degrees, and the sole of the foot facing the ceiling. The thigh of the lifted leg is parallel to the floor, and the spine remains neutral with the core engaged, visibly contracting the hamstrings and gluteus maximus.

exercises.name: Tibialis Anterior Strengthening
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with your feet flat on the floor, knees bent at 90 degrees. Your back is against the chair and core is engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: You remain seated upright with your back against the chair and core engaged, knees bent at 90 degrees. Your heels are firmly on the floor, with the balls of your feet and toes pointing upwards, directed towards your shins. The tibialis anterior muscle is maximally engaged, and the calf muscles are visibly stretched.

exercises.name: Lateral Band Walks with Dumbbells
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, knees slightly bent in a quarter-squat position. Your chest is up and core is engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your leading foot is stepped out to the side, creating a stance significantly wider than shoulder-width, with both knees maintaining the quarter-squat bend. Dumbbells are still held at your sides, chest up, and core engaged. The gluteus medius and minimus of both hips are actively engaged, and a slight stretch is present in the adductors of the trailing leg.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Lifts
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with your back against the backrest, feet flat on the floor, and knees bent at 90 degrees. Your posture is tall and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your torso remains upright against the backrest, core engaged. One leg is extended straight forward, with the knee fully straightened and the heel lifted off the floor, the quadriceps of that leg visibly contracted.

exercises.name: Hip Flexor Stretches
exercises.pose_description: Kneel on one knee with the other leg stepped forward, foot flat on the ground. Keep your torso upright.
exercises.end_pose_description: The pelvis is positioned anterior to the kneeling knee, with the front leg's knee deeply bent directly over the ankle. Your torso remains upright, visibly stretching the hip flexors of the kneeling leg.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Internal Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and elbow bent to 90 degrees at your side, holding a resistance band with both hands. Keep your upper arm stationary against your ribcage throughout the movement.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body remains upright with feet shoulder-width apart, with the active arm's upper arm pressed against the ribcage and elbow bent at 90 degrees. Its forearm is internally rotated, with the hand holding one end of the resistance band positioned across the front of the body towards the navel, while the other hand firmly holds the opposite end of the band, held taut. The subscapularis and pectoralis major muscles are visibly engaged, and the posterior deltoid and infraspinatus are stretched.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Horizontal Abduction
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended in front of you at shoulder height, holding a resistance band stretched between your hands. Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
exercises.end_pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, with your arms extended out to your sides at shoulder height, holding the resistance band maximally stretched between your hands. A slight bend is maintained in your elbows. The posterior deltoids and rhomboids are visibly contracted, while the chest muscles are stretched.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Row
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart on a resistance band, holding the ends with both hands and arms extended downward in front of you. Maintain a neutral spine and slight knee bend throughout the movement.
exercises.end_pose_description: Standing with feet shoulder-width apart on the resistance band, both hands are pulled back to the sides of your torso, near your hips. Your elbows are bent sharply and pointing directly backward, with your shoulder blades strongly retracted and squeezed together. The latissimus dorsi, rhomboids, trapezius, and biceps are visibly contracted, creating definition in your upper back and arms.

exercises.name: Doorway Shoulder Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Stand in a doorway with your right arm raised to 90 degrees and forearm resting against the doorframe. Position your body so you face the doorframe.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your torso is now angled forward, extending past the plane of the doorframe, while your right arm remains pressed against the doorframe. A deep stretch is felt through the anterior deltoid and pectoralis major muscles of your right shoulder and chest.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Shoulder Flexion
exercises.pose_description: Stand on a resistance band with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the ends at your sides with arms extended downward. Maintain good posture with shoulders relaxed.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your body maintains good posture with feet shoulder-width apart on the resistance band. Your arms are extended straight forward and slightly upward, reaching approximately eye level, with hands still holding the band ends and the anterior deltoids visibly engaged.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Lateral Raise
exercises.pose_description: Stand on a resistance band with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the ends at your sides with arms extended downward and a slight elbow bend. Keep your core engaged and posture upright.
exercises.end_pose_description: Core is engaged and posture is upright. Your arms are extended horizontally out to the sides, with a slight elbow bend, forming a "T" shape with your torso, and your hands holding the band ends are level with your shoulders. The deltoid muscles are visibly contracted and the upper trapezius may also be engaged.

exercises.name: Supine Shoulder External Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with your affected shoulder abducted to 90 degrees and elbow bent to 90 degrees, palm facing your head. Keep your upper arm perpendicular to your body.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your affected shoulder is abducted to 90 degrees and your elbow is bent to 90 degrees, with your upper arm perpendicular to your body. Your forearm is externally rotated, pointing downwards towards your feet, and your palm faces your feet; the posterior rotator cuff muscles are visibly engaged, and the anterior shoulder muscles are stretched.

exercises.name: Prone Shoulder I-Y-T Raises
exercises.pose_description: Lie face-down with your forehead resting on a rolled towel and arms at your sides with palms facing down. Engage your core to stabilize your torso.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your forehead remains on the towel. Both arms are straight, angled upwards and outwards from your head to form a 'Y' shape, with thumbs pointing towards the ceiling. Your shoulder blades are visibly retracted and depressed, engaging the posterior deltoids, rhomboids, and lower trapezius muscles. Your core remains engaged to stabilize your torso.

exercises.name: Scapular Wall Slides
exercises.pose_description: Stand with your back against a wall with feet about 12 inches away, knees slightly bent. Place your arms against the wall at shoulder height with elbows bent to 90 degrees.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your arms are fully extended overhead, pressed against the wall, with elbows straight or nearly straight. Hands are positioned directly above the head, with the upper trapezius and serratus anterior visibly engaged and the chest muscles subtly stretched.

exercises.name: Prone Shoulder Blade Squeezes
exercises.pose_description: Lie face-down with your forehead on a rolled towel and arms at your sides, palms facing down. Keep your legs straight and relaxed on the ground.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your forehead rests on the rolled towel, and your arms are slightly lifted off the ground, remaining close to your sides with palms facing down. Your legs are straight and relaxed on the ground, while your shoulder blades are maximally retracted and depressed, visibly engaging the rhomboids and middle trapezius and lengthening the chest muscles.

exercises.name: Supine Shoulder Blade Retractions
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Place your arms at 90 degrees to your body with elbows slightly bent and palms facing up.
exercises.end_pose_description: You are lying on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, with your chest lifted slightly as your shoulder blades are drawn firmly together. Your arms remain at 90 degrees to your body with elbows slightly bent and palms facing up, and the muscles of your mid-back, including the rhomboids and middle trapezius, are fully engaged.

exercises.name: Posterior Shoulder Doorway Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Stand in a doorway with your affected arm raised and forearm against the doorframe at 90 degrees. Position your elbow at shoulder height with your palm facing forward.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your torso is leaned forward through the doorway, with your chest past the doorframe, while your affected arm's forearm remains pressed firmly against the doorframe at 90 degrees. The elbow is at shoulder height, palm forward, and the posterior deltoid, infraspinatus, and teres minor muscles of the affected shoulder are visibly stretched.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge with Dumbbell
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, and a dumbbell resting across your hips. Your arms should be at your sides with palms down for stability.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your hips are maximally elevated towards the ceiling, forming a straight line from your shoulders through your hips to your knees, with the dumbbell still resting across your hips at this highest point. Your glutes and hamstrings are strongly contracted, and your feet remain flat on the floor, hip-width apart, with your arms at your sides for stability.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Deadlift with Dumbbell
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright on your left leg holding a dumbbell in your right hand at your side with a slight knee bend. Keep your core engaged and shoulders back.
exercises.end_pose_description: The torso is hinged forward at the hips, nearly parallel to the floor, with the back straight and the left glute and hamstring visibly engaged. The right leg is extended straight backward, forming a line from the head to the right heel, while the right arm hangs straight down, the dumbbell close to the floor. The erector spinae muscles of the back are visibly engaged, and the hamstring of the standing left leg is under stretch.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with arms extended. Engage your core and maintain a neutral spine with a slight forward hinge at the hips.
exercises.end_pose_description: Maintain the slight forward hip hinge and neutral spine, with your core engaged. The dumbbells are held close to your sides, near the lower ribcage, with elbows bent and pulled back beyond the plane of the torso. Your shoulder blades are visibly retracted and depressed, indicating strong engagement of the latissimus dorsi, rhomboids, and biceps.

exercises.name: Pallof Press with Dumbbell
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell at chest height with both hands, perpendicular to your torso. Keep your core tight and shoulders squared forward.
exercises.end_pose_description: With feet shoulder-width apart, the dumbbell is now held straight out in front of the body at chest height, arms fully extended. The torso and shoulders remain squared forward, resisting any rotational pull. The deep core muscles, especially the obliques and transversus abdominis, are maximally engaged and braced to maintain this stable position.

exercises.name: Quadruped Hip Circle
exercises.pose_description: Start on your hands and knees with a neutral spine, wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. Lift one knee slightly off the ground.
exercises.end_pose_description: Maintain a neutral spine with wrists under shoulders. The lifted knee is positioned high and wide, with the working thigh nearly parallel to the floor and the hip maximally abducted and externally rotated. The gluteus medius and maximus are visibly contracted, while the hip adductors and internal rotators are stretched.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry with Dumbbell
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side with your arm extended, shoulders level and squared. Engage your core to prevent side bending.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body stands upright, arm extended at the side, holding the dumbbell, with shoulders level and squared and hips horizontally aligned. The obliques and quadratus lumborum on the side opposite the dumbbell are visibly contracted, and the erector spinae muscles along the back are engaged, maintaining a neutral spine. The upper trapezius and deltoids on the loaded side also show engagement, stabilizing the shoulder.

exercises.name: Seated Ankle Plantarflexion with Resistance Band
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with your injured leg extended in front of you. Loop a resistance band around the ball of your foot, holding the ends in your hands.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your injured leg remains extended in front of you, with your body upright in the chair. Your foot is pointed downwards, away from your shin, against the taut resistance band. The calf muscles (gastrocnemius and soleus) are visibly contracted, and the muscles on the front of your shin are elongated.

exercises.name: Lateral Ankle Inversion with Resistance Band
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with your injured leg extended or bent at the knee. Loop a resistance band around the forefoot and hold the ends with your hands.
exercises.end_pose_description: The injured foot is rotated inwards at the ankle, with the sole facing the midline of the body, and the resistance band is taut. The tibialis anterior and tibialis posterior muscles on the inner shin are visibly engaged, while the peroneal muscles on the outer ankle are stretched.

exercises.name: Lateral Ankle Eversion with Resistance Band
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with your injured leg extended or bent at the knee. Loop a resistance band around the forefoot and hold the ends with your hands.
exercises.end_pose_description: The injured foot is positioned so its sole faces outwards and slightly upwards, creating tension in the resistance band looped around the forefoot. The outer ankle muscles, specifically the peroneus longus and brevis, are visibly contracted and shortened on the lateral side of the lower leg.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Balance on Foam Pad
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright on a foam balance pad or unstable surface with feet hip-width apart, arms at your sides. Distribute your weight evenly on both feet.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body is balanced upright on one foot on the foam pad, with the opposite knee bent and the foot hovering just above the pad. The standing leg's knee is slightly flexed, and the arms remain at the sides. The ankle stabilizers of the standing foot, core muscles, and hip abductors are visibly engaged to maintain equilibrium.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Adduction
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your unaffected side with both legs extended and a resistance band looped around both thighs just above the knees. Keep your torso stable and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lie on your unaffected side with both legs extended, the resistance band taut and the top leg firmly pressed against the bottom leg. Both legs touch along their entire length, and the inner thigh muscles of the top leg are visibly contracted. Your torso remains stable with your core engaged.

exercises.name: Prone Hip Internal Rotation Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lie face-down on the floor with your forearms supporting your upper body. Bend one knee and bring that foot toward the opposite side of your body.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lie face-down on the floor with your forearms supporting your upper body. The bent knee remains grounded, and that foot is positioned fully across the opposite side of your body, with the lower leg resting on the floor. The hip external rotators and groin muscles of the bent leg are maximally stretched.

exercises.name: Seated Figure-4 Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright on the floor with both legs extended in front of you. Bend one knee and place that ankle across the opposite leg's thigh, forming a figure-4 shape.
exercises.end_pose_description: The torso is inclined forward from the hips, with the chest positioned over the shin of the bent leg. The spine maintains a straight, neutral position, and the shoulders are relaxed. A visible stretch is apparent in the gluteal muscles and piriformis of the bent leg.

exercises.name: Finger Isolation Lifts
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your forearm resting on a table, palm down with fingers extended. Keep all fingers relaxed and in contact with the table.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your forearm remains resting on the table, palm down, with the index finger maximally lifted off the surface. The remaining fingers stay relaxed and fully in contact with the table, with the extensor muscles on the back of the forearm visibly engaged.

exercises.name: Forearm Pronation and Supination
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your elbow bent to 90 degrees and tucked against your body, palm facing up (supinated position). Keep your forearm steady.
exercises.end_pose_description: Sit with your elbow bent to 90 degrees and tucked against your body, palm facing down (pronated position). The pronator muscles of the forearm are engaged, while the supinator muscles are stretched.

exercises.name: Upper Extremity Pendulum Swings
exercises.pose_description: Stand with your affected arm hanging relaxed at your side. Bend slightly at the waist to allow your arm to swing freely.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your affected arm is positioned forward and elevated in front of your body, with the elbow extended. Your shoulder is in maximal comfortable flexion, and the posterior shoulder muscles are visibly stretched. Your torso maintains its slight bend at the waist.

exercises.name: Neck and Shoulder Relaxation
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with good posture. Keep your shoulders relaxed and your arms resting in your lap.
exercises.end_pose_description: The head is gently tilted to the right, bringing the right ear close to the right shoulder. The left shoulder remains relaxed and lowered away from the ear. A gentle stretch is evident along the left side of the neck and into the left upper trapezius muscle.

exercises.name: Step-Ups with Dumbbells
exercises.pose_description: Stand facing a step or low platform (12-18 inches) holding dumbbells at your sides with arms extended. Plant your foot firmly on the step with your whole foot making contact.
exercises.end_pose_description: Stand fully upright on the step, with your lead foot firmly planted and its leg fully extended. The trailing leg is positioned onto the step, with its foot lightly touching or hovering just above the platform. The quadriceps and glutes of the lead leg are visibly contracted, while the hip flexors of the trailing leg are engaged. Dumbbells remain at your sides with arms extended.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Deadlifts with Dumbbells
exercises.pose_description: Stand on one leg while holding dumbbells at your sides, with a slight bend in your standing knee. Your non-working leg is relaxed and your gaze is fixed forward to maintain balance.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your torso is hinged forward at the hip, nearly parallel to the floor, with the dumbbells hanging straight down towards the ground, and your standing knee maintains its slight bend. Your non-working leg is extended straight back and level with your torso, with the hamstrings of the standing leg visibly stretched and the glutes and erector spinae engaged; your gaze is fixed on the floor.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Curtsy Lunges
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright holding dumbbells at your sides with feet hip-width apart and your weight evenly distributed. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture throughout the movement.
exercises.end_pose_description: One leg is stepped diagonally back and across behind the other, with both knees deeply bent. The front thigh is nearly parallel to the floor and the front knee is aligned over the ankle, while the back knee is lowered close to the ground behind the front foot. The torso remains upright, and dumbbells are held at the sides. The gluteus maximus, quadriceps, and hamstrings of the front leg are visibly engaged, and the hip flexors of the back leg are stretched.

exercises.name: Prone I-Y-T Raises
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on a bench or floor with arms at your sides and forehead resting on a towel. Your legs are extended with toes on the ground for stability.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your torso remains face down, and your forehead is lightly touching the towel. Your arms are extended straight out to your sides, perpendicular to your body, at shoulder height. Your hands are held a few inches off the floor or bench, with palms facing down and elbows straight. The upper back muscles, including the rhomboids and rear deltoids, are visibly contracted and engaged.

exercises.name: Neck Isometric Holds
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with good posture and your hands placed against the side of your head. Your neck is in a neutral position looking straight ahead.
exercises.end_pose_description: You maintain an upright posture in the chair, with your right hand pressing firmly against the right side of your head. Your neck remains in a neutral position, looking straight ahead, as if attempting to bend towards your right shoulder. The right sternocleidomastoid, scalene muscles, and other lateral neck flexors are visibly engaged and tensed.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck Flyes
exercises.pose_description: Sit on a reverse pec deck machine with your chest against the pad and hands gripping the handles at shoulder height. Your shoulders are relaxed and arms are bent slightly.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your arms are extended straight out to your sides, slightly bent at the elbows, and aligned horizontally with your shoulders. Your shoulder blades are strongly retracted and squeezed together, pulling your hands and the handles as far back as the machine allows. The muscles of your posterior deltoids, rhomboids, and middle trapezius are visibly contracted, creating a defined and powerful upper back.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Rows
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with feet flat on the floor and loop a resistance band around a fixed point at chest height. Hold both ends of the band with arms extended forward at shoulder width.
exercises.end_pose_description: Sit upright with feet flat on the floor, the resistance band taut and pulled towards the body. Elbows are bent and pulled back, close to the torso, with hands positioned near the lower rib cage, still holding both ends of the band. The shoulder blades are squeezed together, and the latissimus dorsi and rhomboids are visibly contracted in the upper back.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Pull-Aparts
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold a resistance band with both hands at shoulder height, arms extended in front of you. The band should be taut but not stretched at the starting position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms extended out to the sides and slightly behind the torso, holding the fully stretched resistance band. The shoulder blades are visibly retracted, with the rhomboids and rear deltoids engaged, while the chest muscles are stretched.

exercises.name: Upper Back Strengthening with Band
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and hold a looped resistance band at waist level with both hands. Your arms should be straight down with a slight bend at the elbows and the band at rest.
exercises.end_pose_description: The hands are pulled back towards the sides of your upper abdomen, with elbows sharply bent and tucked close to your body, stretching the resistance band taut. Your shoulder blades are powerfully retracted, visibly engaging the rhomboids, middle trapezius, and posterior deltoids.

exercises.name: Scapular Retractions
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with your back against a chair or wall, arms at your sides with elbows bent at 90 degrees. Hold a resistance band with both hands, maintaining slight tension in the band.
exercises.end_pose_description: Sit upright with your back against a chair or wall, your shoulder blades retracted and squeezed together. Your elbows are pulled backward, moving behind your torso, and the resistance band is significantly stretched with hands wider apart. The rhomboids and middle trapezius in your upper back are visibly engaged, and your chest muscles are stretched.

exercises.name: Posterior Neck Stretch with Band
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright and loop a resistance band around the back of your head at about ear level, holding both ends of the band in your hands. Keep your neck in a neutral position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Maintain the upright seated position with the resistance band looped around the back of your head, held by your hands. Your head is in full flexion, with your chin resting close to your chest, creating a deep stretch along the posterior neck muscles.

exercises.name: Thoracic Extension with Band
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with a resistance band looped around your upper back at shoulder blade height, holding both ends across your chest. Your shoulders should be relaxed and your spine neutral.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your upper back is deeply arched into extension, and your chest is pressed forward against the taut resistance band. Your shoulders are retracted, and your head is aligned with your extended thoracic spine, with a slight upward gaze. The erector spinae and rhomboids are engaged, while the pectoralis muscles across your chest are visibly stretched.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Reverse Fly
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and slightly bent knees, holding a resistance band with both hands at waist level in front of your body. Your arms should be extended straight with a slight bend at the elbows.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your feet remain shoulder-width apart with slightly bent knees. Your arms are extended straight, with a slight bend at the elbows, positioned out to your sides, forming a 'T' shape with your body. The resistance band is stretched taut across your chest, and your shoulder blades are squeezed together, visibly engaging the posterior deltoids, rhomboids, and trapezius, with the pectorals stretched across the front.

exercises.name: Scapular Squeeze (Prone)
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on a firm surface with arms at your sides, palms facing down. Your forehead rests on a rolled towel to keep your neck neutral.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your shoulder blades are actively drawn together and depressed towards your hips, with a noticeable contraction of the muscles between them. Your arms are slightly lifted off the surface, maintaining palms-down orientation. The rhomboids, middle, and lower trapezius are visibly engaged.

exercises.name: Seated Upper Back Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with your feet flat on the floor. Clasp your hands together in front of your chest.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your arms are extended straight forward, with your clasped hands pushed away from your body. Your upper back is rounded, creating a gentle curve in the thoracic spine. Your head is relaxed, with your chin dropped towards your chest, and your shoulder blades are pulled apart. This position deeply stretches the muscles of the upper back, including the rhomboids, trapezius, and erector spinae.

exercises.name: Supine Shoulder Blade Retraction
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Arms are extended straight up toward the ceiling with palms facing each other.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Arms remain extended straight up toward the ceiling with palms facing each other, but the shoulder blades are drawn together and down toward the spine, with the shoulders lowered towards the floor. The rhomboids and middle trapezius are engaged, and the chest muscles are stretched.

exercises.name: Thoracic Spine Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Start on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. Your spine is neutral and core is engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: One hand is positioned behind the head with the elbow pointed directly towards the ceiling. The head is turned, gazing upwards, and the upper body is rotated through the thoracic spine. The supporting arm remains stable with the wrist under the shoulder, while the muscles of the thoracic spine and obliques on the side of the raised elbow are engaged, and the opposite obliques are stretched.

exercises.name: Cervical Retraction with Resistance
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with good posture and place your hand against your chin. Your neck is in a neutral position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your head is maximally retracted straight back, tucking the chin to create a gentle double chin. Your hand remains pressed against your chin, and the deep neck flexors are visibly contracted.

exercises.name: Thoracic Spine Extension Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright and clasp your hands behind your head with your elbows wide. Your feet are flat on the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: The upper back shows a gentle arch, with the thoracic spine extended backward. The head is tilted slightly rearward, and the chest is visibly open. Your hands remain clasped behind your head with elbows wide, feet flat on the floor. The thoracic spine extensors are actively stretched.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shrugs
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, holding dumbbells at your sides with arms extended. Your shoulders are relaxed and your chest is up.
exercises.end_pose_description: You remain standing upright with feet hip-width apart, holding dumbbells at your sides with arms extended. Your shoulders are elevated high, nearly touching your ears, with the upper trapezius muscles visibly contracted and bulging. Your chest is still up.

exercises.name: Postural Wall Hold
exercises.pose_description: Stand with your back against a wall with heels, glutes, and shoulders all touching the wall. Your neck should be in neutral alignment with your head also touching the wall.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body remains against the wall with heels, glutes, shoulders, and head all touching, and the neck in neutral alignment. The lower back is actively pressed flat against the wall, with visibly engaged abdominal muscles and glutes, while the erector spinae and rhomboids subtly maintain upper back contact.

exercises.name: Neck Isometric Hold
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with perfect posture and place your hand against one side of your head. Your neck is in a neutral position.
exercises.end_pose_description: You maintain your upright seated posture with your hand firmly against the side of your head. Your neck remains in a neutral position, but the lateral muscles on the side of your head where your hand is placed are visibly contracted and tensed, resisting the force of your hand.

exercises.name: Prone Hip Extensions
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on the floor with your forehead resting on your hands and legs extended straight behind you. Keep your core engaged to prevent lower back arching.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your forehead remains resting on your hands, and your legs are extended straight behind you, elevated a few inches off the floor. Your glutes and hamstrings are strongly contracted, holding your legs in this elevated position, while your core remains engaged to prevent excessive lower back arching.

exercises.name: Quadriceps Stretching
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and use one hand on a wall or object for balance. Bend one knee and bring your foot toward your glutes.
exercises.end_pose_description: The bent knee is positioned so the foot rests against the glutes. The thigh of the bent leg is held vertically, and a visible stretch is apparent in the quadriceps muscle along the front of that thigh.

exercises.name: Hamstring Stretching
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with one leg extended on the floor and the other knee bent with foot flat. Use a strap, towel, or your hands around the bent knee's thigh.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body remains supine with one leg extended flat on the floor. The other leg is fully straightened at the knee and lifted directly upwards, perpendicular to the floor, or gently pulled slightly past this point towards the head. The hands or a strap apply a steady pull on the lifted leg's thigh or calf. The hamstring muscles along the entire back of this lifted thigh are visibly elongated and taut, indicating the peak of the stretch.

exercises.name: Prone Shoulder Squeeze
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on a mat with your forehead resting on a towel and arms at your sides, palms facing down. Keep your legs extended with toes pointing down.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your forehead rests on the towel, and your legs are extended with toes pointing down. Your shoulder blades are drawn together toward your spine and slightly downward. Your arms are slightly elevated off the mat, with palms facing down, and the muscles of your upper back, including the rhomboids and middle trapezius, are visibly engaged.

exercises.name: Band Rows
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold a resistance band at arm's length in front of you with both hands. Keep your core engaged and maintain a neutral spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your feet remain shoulder-width apart, core engaged, and spine neutral. Your hands are pulled back towards your torso, with elbows bent and the resistance band taut and close to your body. Your shoulder blades are visibly retracted, highlighting the contracted latissimus dorsi, rhomboids, and trapezius muscles in your back, along with engaged biceps.

exercises.name: Seated Thoracic Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright on a chair or bench with feet flat on the floor. Cross your arms across your chest, with your right hand touching your left shoulder and left hand touching your right shoulder.
exercises.end_pose_description: The torso is fully rotated to the right, with the shoulders and chest aligned toward the right side. The lower body, including the hips and feet, remains fixed and facing forward, and the arms stay crossed with hands on opposite shoulders. The core muscles, including the obliques and erector spinae on the right, are visibly engaged, while the muscles on the left side of the back and torso are stretched.

exercises.name: Doorway Pectoral Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Stand in a doorway with your right arm raised to 90 degrees, placing your forearm against the door frame. Your body faces straight ahead with good posture.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your body is positioned forward through the doorway, maintaining your right forearm pressed firmly against the door frame. Your chest extends past your right shoulder, indicating a stretch across the right pectoral muscle and anterior deltoid.

exercises.name: Overhead Shoulder Press
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding dumbbells at shoulder height with elbows bent at 90 degrees. Your core is engaged and your spine is neutral.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your feet remain shoulder-width apart, and the dumbbells are held directly overhead with fully extended arms. Your elbows are straight, and your shoulders are elevated towards your ears, visibly engaging the deltoids and triceps. Your core remains engaged and your spine neutral.

exercises.name: Chest Opener Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and interlace your fingers behind your back at hip level. Your shoulders are relaxed and your posture is upright.
exercises.end_pose_description: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, your interlaced hands lifted several inches away from your glutes. Your shoulders are visibly retracted and depressed, opening the chest and stretching the pectorals and anterior deltoids.

exercises.name: Neck Flexor Release
exercises.pose_description: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and shoulders relaxed. Place one hand gently on top of your head near the opposite ear.
exercises.end_pose_description: The head is gently tilted sideways towards the hand's side, with the ear approaching the shoulder, and slightly extended backward. The chin is rotated towards the opposite side of the chest, resulting in the gaze directed diagonally upward. The sternocleidomastoid muscle on the side opposite the hand is visibly lengthened and stretched.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Dumbbell Deadlift
exercises.pose_description: Stand on one leg with a slight knee bend, holding a dumbbell in the opposite hand at your side. Your standing leg is stable and your core is engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Stand upright, balanced on one leg with a slight knee bend, the dumbbell held in the opposite hand at your side. Your glutes and hamstrings are visibly engaged, your back is straight, and your core is braced.

exercises.name: Wall Angel Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Stand with your back against a wall, feet about 6 inches away from the base. Your arms are at shoulder height with elbows bent at 90 degrees against the wall.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your back and head remain against the wall, with feet 6 inches from the base. Your arms are raised overhead, with the back of your wrists, forearms, and upper arms pressed firmly against the wall. The elbows are slightly bent, fingers pointing towards the ceiling, stretching the chest and front of the shoulders.

exercises.name: Thoracic Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Begin on hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips. Place one hand behind your head with elbow pointing out to the side.
exercises.end_pose_description: The hands and knees remain in their starting position with the hand still behind the head. The elbow from that hand points directly towards the ceiling, indicating maximum thoracic rotation. The spinal rotators and obliques are engaged, while the chest and side muscles on the opposite side appear stretched.

exercises.name: Butterfly Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with the soles of your feet together and knees falling out to the sides, forming a diamond shape with your legs. Keep your back straight and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: The torso is gently folded forward from the hips, with the soles of the feet remaining together and knees pressed further towards the floor. The back remains straight and long, showing a deep stretch in the inner thighs and groin.

exercises.name: Shoulder Crossover Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides in a neutral position. Maintain an upright posture with shoulders relaxed.
exercises.end_pose_description: Stand with feet hip-width apart and an upright posture. One arm is extended straight across the chest at shoulder height, with the hand reaching towards the opposite side. The other arm is bent at the elbow, with its forearm resting against the upper arm of the extended arm, creating a deep cross-body stretch. The posterior deltoid and rotator cuff muscles of the extended arm are visibly stretched.

exercises.name: Spinal Twist
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, arms spread out to the sides in a T position. Keep your back flat against the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: The knees are bent and stacked, resting on the floor to the right side, with the feet stacked beneath them. The upper back and shoulders are flat on the floor, arms spread in a T position, while the lower back is lifted from the floor, and the head is turned to the left. The spine and glutes on the left side are stretched, and the right obliques are visibly engaged.

exercises.name: Banded Hip Abduction
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and a resistance band looped around both legs just above the knees. Keep your core engaged and hands on your hips for balance.
exercises.end_pose_description: Maintain an upright torso with one foot planted firmly on the ground. The other leg is extended directly out to the side, away from the body, stretching the resistance band taut. Your hips remain level, core engaged, and hands on your hips. The gluteus medius and minimus of the extended leg are visibly contracted.

exercises.name: Banded Clamshells
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your right side with a resistance band looped around your thighs just above the knees and your knees bent at 45 degrees. Stack your hips and keep your core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: The left knee is externally rotated and raised significantly away from the right knee, while the heels stay pressed together. The hips remain stacked and still, and the core is engaged. The resistance band is taut, and the gluteus medius and gluteus minimus of the left leg are visibly contracted.

exercises.name: Banded Hip Bridge
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, and a resistance band looped around your thighs just above the knees. Place arms at your sides with palms down.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your hips are elevated, creating a straight line from your shoulders through your hips to your knees. Knees remain bent, pushing against the resistance band to keep feet flat and hip-width apart on the floor. Arms are at your sides with palms down, and the glutes and hamstrings are visibly engaged while the hip flexors are stretched.

exercises.name: 90-90 Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Kneel on your right knee with your left foot planted in front of you, both legs bent at 90 degrees. Keep your torso upright and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your torso is inclined forward over your left leg, with your left knee bent at an acute angle and your foot remaining planted. Your right hip is extended, stretching the hip flexors on the front of your right thigh, while your right knee remains on the ground and your torso stays upright with core engaged.

exercises.name: Banded Lateral Walk
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet hip-width apart and a resistance band looped around your legs just above the knees. Slightly bend your knees and keep your torso upright with hands on your hips.
exercises.end_pose_description: The feet are positioned wide apart, with one foot laterally separated from the other; the stance is significantly wider than hip-width. Knees are slightly bent, and the torso is upright with hands on hips. The resistance band is taut and stretched across the thighs, with the gluteus medius visibly engaged on the outer hips of both legs.

exercises.name: Thoracic Rotation in Quadruped
exercises.pose_description: Start on your hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips. Place your left hand behind your head with elbow pointing out to the side.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your right hand remains under your shoulder and knees remain under your hips. Your torso is rotated significantly to the left and upwards, with your left elbow pointing directly towards the ceiling and your head looking upwards, visibly engaging the muscles of your left mid-back and obliques and stretching the muscles of your right mid-back.

exercises.name: Standing Doorway Chest Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Stand facing a doorway or wall with your right arm raised to 90 degrees with elbow bent, forearm vertical. Step your right foot forward into the doorway.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body is leaning forward through the doorway, with the right arm's forearm pressed against the doorframe. The right shoulder is horizontally extended, and the chest muscles (pectorals) are visibly stretched.

exercises.name: Thread the Needle Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Cross your right ankle over your left knee, creating a figure-4 position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Both hands clasp the back of your left thigh, with the left knee drawn towards your chest while maintaining the figure-4 position. Your right arm extends through the opening created by your legs, and the right gluteal muscles and outer hip are visibly stretched.

exercises.name: Standing Trunk Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent. Cross your arms over your chest with each hand on the opposite shoulder.
exercises.end_pose_description: Feet are shoulder-width apart and knees are slightly bent. The torso is maximally rotated to the right, with the head turned to look over the right shoulder. Arms are crossed over the chest with each hand on the opposite shoulder. The right oblique muscles are visibly engaged, and the left oblique muscles are stretched.

exercises.name: Tall Kneeling Quadriceps Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Kneel on the floor with your knees hip-width apart and torso upright. Hands can be placed on your thighs or behind you for balance.
exercises.end_pose_description: Your glutes are lowered to rest on your heels, with the tops of your feet pressed flat against the floor. Your torso maintains its upright posture, and your hands remain positioned for balance. The muscles along the front of your shins and the top of your feet are visibly elongated and stretched.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell vertically at chest height with both hands. Keep your chest up and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body is in a deep squat position, with hips descended until the thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below, and knees deeply bent, tracking over the feet. The chest remains upright with the dumbbell held at chest height, as the glutes and quadriceps are highly engaged, and the calves are stretched.

exercises.name: Ankle Circles with Single Leg Balance
exercises.pose_description: Stand on one leg with a slight knee bend, arms out to sides for balance. Keep your standing leg stable and engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: The standing leg maintains its slight knee bend and engagement, with arms remaining out to the sides for balance. The non-standing foot is pointed downwards, with the sole turned outwards, visibly engaging the calf and outer shin muscles as the ankle reaches peak plantarflexion and eversion.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Ankle Mobility Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Assume a half-kneeling position with one foot forward and hands on the ground. The forward foot should be flat on the ground with knee bent at 90 degrees.
exercises.end_pose_description: The forward knee is positioned significantly forward, extending past the toes, with the heel of the forward foot firmly planted on the ground. The shin of the forward leg is angled acutely forward, demonstrating deep ankle dorsiflexion and a visible stretch through the calf muscles. Hands remain on the ground for support.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Lunges
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet together holding dumbbells at your sides, chest up and core engaged. Maintain an upright posture with weight distributed evenly.
exercises.end_pose_description: One leg is fully extended to the side with the foot flat on the ground, while the other leg is bent at the knee, with the thigh parallel to the floor and the knee directly over the ankle. The torso leans slightly forward from the hips, maintaining a proud chest and engaged core, with dumbbells hanging naturally at the sides. The glutes and quadriceps of the bent leg are engaged, and the adductors of the extended leg are visibly stretched.

exercises.name: Seated Toe Touches with Flexion/Extension
